The Hebrew verb is related to a word for “horn” or “ray.” St Jerome's Latin translation read “horned,” which is why Moses is painted and carved with horns, as in Michelangelo's statue. The Hebrew means he shone with rays of light.
The veil.

Moses veiled his face after speaking with the people and unveiled it when he went into the Lord's presence. St Paul uses the image: in Christ, Christians look at the glory of the Lord “with unveiled faces” and are transformed (2 Corinthians 3:12–18).
“Afraid to come near.”
Holiness both frightens and attracts. The saints are not distant; they are people through whom God's light is allowed to reach others.
“Moses and Aaron among his priests.”
Psalm 99 names three who called on the Lord and were answered: Moses, Aaron and Samuel. Intercessors who spoke with God are the Old Testament pattern of the saints who pray for us.
Treasure in a field.

In a land without banks, people buried valuables in the ground and sometimes died without recovering them. Finding such a treasure in someone else's field was a stroke of fortune. The parable's point is not the finder's cleverness but his joy and the readiness to give all.
The pearl.
Pearls were among the most precious goods of the ancient world, traded across the seas from the Gulf and the Indian Ocean. A merchant who knew pearls could recognise one of great value at once.
Franciscan Clarist Congregation.
A Syro-Malabar religious congregation of sisters following the Franciscan spirit, with its mother house in Kerala. Alphonsa joined its convent at Bharananganam in Kottayam district in 1927.
“Of the Immaculate Conception.”
The name she took as a religious honours the doctrine, defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854, that Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception (Catechism 490–493).
The first woman of Indian origin canonised.

St Alphonsa was canonised in St Peter's Square on 12 October 2008, together with three other saints. She is a daughter of the Syro-Malabar Church, an Eastern Catholic Church in full communion with Rome, and a saint honoured by the whole Church in India, whatever the rite.
altar: St Alphonsa lived her last years in pain, and she said that she offered it with the Cross of Jesus. This is what happens at every Mass. The one sacrifice of Calvary is made present on the altar, and we are invited to place on the paten our own struggles, illnesses and unseen sacrifices so that they are united to Christ's offering (Catechism 618, 1368). Nothing offered in love is wasted; the grain of wheat that dies bears fruit.

Moses came down with a shining face from speaking with God. After Holy Communion we too carry the Lord himself in our hearts, and, like Moses, we may not know that something of his light is on our faces. Let us go out from Mass as people who have been in his presence, and let others see it by our gentleness and joy.
outline: Opening
Ask: when did you last meet someone who had clearly been with God, and what did you notice about them?
Point 1 · A shining face
Moses does not know his face shines; he veils it and unveils it before God.
Point 2 · The treasure and the pearl
The kingdom is found with joy, and the finder gives all.
Point 3 · The grain that dies
Alphonsa's hidden suffering offered in love bears fruit in Kerala and the world.
Closing image
The tomb at Bharananganam, with a line of pilgrims and a single lighted candle.
Take-home line
“Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”
live: Offer one hidden thing
Choose one small pain, tiredness or disappointment today and offer it quietly to Jesus for someone by name, as St Alphonsa taught by her life.
Show the light
Be gentle with someone who is hard to deal with this week, and let them see in you something of the peace you find in prayer.
Find the pearl
Ask yourself what you would give up to follow Christ more fully, and take one step this week: a confession, a regular time of prayer, an act of generosity.
Visit a pilgrim place
If you can, visit the tomb of St Alphonsa at Bharananganam or a church dedicated to her, or pray before her picture, asking her for the grace of patient love in suffering.
fathers: St Gregory the Great (Homilies on the Gospels 11, in substance)

The kingdom of heaven is a hidden treasure because it is the desire of heavenly things. One who has found it guards that desire and sells, that is, gives up, all earthly pleasures in order to buy the field of the Gospel life.
St Francis of Assisi (Canticle of the Creatures, in substance)
Praised be you, my Lord, through those who pardon for love of you, and who bear sickness and trial: blessed are those who endure in peace, for by you, Most High, they will be crowned.
St Thérèse of Lisieux (Story of a Soul, in substance)
A hidden life in a convent can be great: she offered every small act and every small suffering for others and for the Church, and trusted that the love given in secret would reach the whole world.
magis: Catechism 2013
All the faithful, in whatever state of life, are called to the fullness of Christian life and to the perfection of love; holiness is the vocation of all.
Catechism 618, 1505
Christ gives suffering a new meaning: it can unite us with his redemptive passion, and he invites his disciples to take up their cross and follow him.
Catechism 922–924
Consecrated virgins and religious give their whole lives to Christ, as a sign of the kingdom and a witness of love for the Church.
Catechism 2544
Jesus asks his disciples to prefer him to everything and everyone, and to renounce all for his sake and the Gospel.
Catechism 828
By canonising some of the faithful, the Church recognises their power of the Spirit of holiness and sustains the hope of the faithful by giving them saints as models and intercessors.
saints: St Alphonsa of the Immaculate Conception (1910–1946)

Born Anna Muttathupadathu at Kudamaloor, Kottayam; a Franciscan Clarist sister of the Syro-Malabar Church at Bharananganam; a hidden life of prayer, teaching and long illness offered in love; died 28 July 1946, aged 35; beatified 8 February 1986; canonised 12 October 2008, the first woman of Indian origin to be canonised and the first canonised saint of the Syro-Malabar Church. Her tomb at Bharananganam is a place of pilgrimage.
This week
29 Jul: Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus (memorial). 30 Jul: St Peter Chrysologus (optional memorial). 31 Jul: St Ignatius of Loyola (memorial).
2027-07-28.prayer: Lord God, you hid the life of St Alphonsa in a quiet convent and let it shine on the whole Church in India. Through her prayers, grant that we too may find the pearl of great value, offer our sufferings in love for others, and carry your light with gentleness, so that those who see us may come near and give glory to you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. St Alphonsa, pray for us.

2027-07-29.title: Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus
readings: The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle
How lovely is your dwelling place, Lord, mighty God
I am the resurrection and the life
2027-07-29.alt: Memorial of Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus, the sister and brother of Bethany and friends of Jesus. Until 2021 the Roman calendar kept only St Martha on 29 July. The first reading is that of the weekday (Week 17, Year I); the Gospel is the proper one, John 11:19–27, with Luke 10:38–42 as the alternative; the weekday Gospel (Matthew 13:47–53) is not used. Mary of Bethany is not to be confused with St Mary Magdalene, whose feast was kept on 22 July. Psalm verses are given in NRSV numbering. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-07-29.verse: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
theo: Moses finishes the work that he began at the foot of Sinai, and the reading says again and again: he did it “as the Lord had commanded Moses.” The tabernacle is set up on the first day of the first month of the second year, a year, almost to the day, after the Exodus. The ark is brought in, the tablets of the covenant are laid inside it, the mercy seat is set above it, and a curtain screens the ark from sight. Then the Lord answers: “the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. Moses was not able to enter.” God has come to live in the middle of his people, and he is too great to be entered or used. When the cloud lifts, Israel moves; when it stays, Israel stays; and by night “fire was in the cloud.” The Psalm is the song of one who longs for such a house: “My soul longs, indeed it faints for the courts of the Lord... Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself... at your altars, O Lord of hosts.” The Church gives us this reading on the day of three friends of Jesus because Bethany was, for him, such a dwelling place: a house where he was welcome.

The proper Gospel of the memorial is from St John. Bethany is “near Jerusalem, some two miles away,” and Lazarus has been dead four days. “Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them.” When she hears that Jesus is coming, Martha goes out to meet him, while Mary stays at home. Martha is practical and honest, and the Gospels show her often at the centre of things. She says what many of us have said at a graveside: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” But she goes on: “even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him.” Jesus tells her, “Your brother will rise again.” She answers with the faith of Israel: “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day.” And Jesus lifts her from a future hope to a present Person: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” Her answer is one of the great confessions of the Gospels, like the one Peter gives at Caesarea Philippi: “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.” St Luke gives the other well-known scene, the alternative Gospel today: Martha “welcomed him into her home,” and was “distracted by her many tasks,” while Mary “sat at the Lord's feet and listened to what he was saying.” Jesus does not scold Martha for serving, but for being “worried and distracted by many things”: “there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.” In St John's account of the supper at Bethany a week before the Passion, all three are together: “Martha served, and Lazarus was one of those at the table with him. Mary took a pound of costly perfume... The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.” Martha serves, Lazarus sits at table as a witness, and Mary anoints. The Church honours them together as a household where Jesus was a friend, since 2021 on one day. Eastern tradition says Lazarus became bishop of Kition in Cyprus, and Western legends place the family in Provence; these are traditions, not Scripture. The Gospels give us the three of them in their home, and that is enough.
outline: Opening
Ask: where do you feel most at home with the Lord, and who has made a home for him in your life?
Point 1 · The dwelling of God
The tabernacle and the glory: God chooses to live among his people.
Point 2 · I am the resurrection
Martha's honest faith, and Jesus' words that turn a distant hope into a Person.
Point 3 · The better part
Serving and listening: Martha and Mary, and the house at Bethany.
Take-home line
“I am the resurrection and the life.”
live: Make room for the Lord (Luke 10:38)
Welcome Jesus into your home today: set aside five minutes at the table or at a window to read a Gospel passage, quietly, as Mary did.
Serve without being distracted (Luke 10:41)
Do one household task today as an act of love for the Lord, and let it be quiet service, without complaint or comparison.
saints: Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany

Friends of Jesus. Martha welcomed him into her home and confessed him as Messiah and Son of God; Mary sat at his feet and anointed him; Lazarus, whom he raised from the dead, never speaks in the Gospels but is a living sign of the resurrection. St Martha is invoked by those who cook, cater and keep house. The Church honours the three together since 2021.
2027-07-29.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were a guest in the home of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, and you wept at the grave of your friend. Be a guest in our homes, and make them places of hospitality, prayer and peace. Teach us Martha's honest faith, Mary's attentive listening and Lazarus's silent witness. You are the resurrection and the life: strengthen our faith and bring our dead into your light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At Mass we meet the Lord who “lived among us” (John 1:14), literally who pitched his tent among us. The tabernacle of the old covenant was filled with the glory of the Lord, but no one could enter it; in the Eucharist the same Lord gives himself to be received. Martha's confession, “I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God,” is the faith we renew each time we say Amen to the Body of Christ. And his words, “I am the resurrection and the life,” are the promise behind the Mass for the dead and every Christian funeral.

2027-07-30.title: Friday of the Seventeenth Week in Ordinary Time · St Peter Chrysologus
readings: These are the appointed festivals of the Lord, the holy convocations
Sing with joy to God our help
Prophets are not without honor except in their own country and in their own house
2027-07-30.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 17 (Year I). The first reading begins the festival calendar of Leviticus, read today and tomorrow. The optional memorial of St Peter Chrysologus, bishop and doctor of the Church, may be kept (liturgical colour white); if it is not kept, green. Psalm verses are given in NRSV numbering.
2027-07-30.verse: And they took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “Prophets are not without honor except in their own country and in their own house.” And he did not do many deeds of power there, because of their unbelief.
theo: The Book of Leviticus opens a calendar. “These are the appointed festivals of the Lord, the holy convocations, which you shall celebrate at the time appointed for them.” Time itself becomes holy. The year of Israel is not a mere wheel of seasons, but a series of meetings with God at fixed hours. First comes the Passover, “on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight,” followed by seven days of unleavened bread, the memorial of the night of the Exodus. Then the first fruits: when the harvest begins, the people bring “the sheaf of the first fruits” to the priest, who raises it before the Lord “on the day after the sabbath.” From that day they “count off seven weeks... fifty days,” and then bring an offering of new grain, the feast of Weeks, which Greek-speaking Jews called Pentecost, “the fiftieth.” Then the Day of Atonement, “you shall deny yourselves,” when the people confessed their sins, and the Feast of Booths, seven days of living in huts of branches in memory of the wilderness. These festivals are God's gifts to Israel, and the Jewish people still keep them with faithfulness; the Church honours them as such and teaches that God's covenant with Israel has never been revoked (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 839). Christians also see in them a pattern that was fulfilled in Christ. He died at Passover; he rose on “the day after the sabbath,” which is the day of the first fruits, and St Paul calls him “the first fruits of those who have died” (1 Corinthians 15:20); fifty days later the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost. The Psalm is the song for such feasts: “Sing aloud to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob. Raise a song, sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp. Blow the trumpet at the new moon, at the full moon, on our festal day. For it is a statute for Israel.”

In the Gospel Jesus comes “to his hometown” of Nazareth and teaches in the synagogue. The people are astounded, but their astonishment does not turn into faith. “Where did this man get this wisdom and these deeds of power? Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary? And are not his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas? And are not all his sisters with us?” They know everything about him except who he is. The “brothers” and “sisters” are, in the language of the Bible, close relatives; the Church has always taught that Mary remained a virgin and that Jesus was her only child (Catechism 499–500). “They took offense at him”: the Greek word means that he became a stumbling block to them. Familiarity can hide holiness; they could not believe that God could be so near, so ordinary, so well known. Jesus answers with a proverb: “Prophets are not without honor except in their own country and in their own house.” Then St Matthew says something sobering: “he did not do many deeds of power there, because of their unbelief.” God does not force his gifts on anyone; where faith is closed, there is little the Lord can do. The two readings belong together. In Leviticus God comes near on the appointed days, and the people have to be ready to meet him. In Nazareth he came near on an ordinary day, in an ordinary man, and they missed him. We should be careful that we do not miss him either, in the Mass we know so well, in the neighbour we think we know, in the daily bread of our own home. St Peter Chrysologus, whom the Church remembers today, was a bishop who knew how to make the familiar words of the Gospel sound new.
outline: Opening
Ask: what is so familiar to you in your faith that you no longer see it?
Point 1 · Holy time
God sets appointed feasts, and meets his people at fixed hours.
Point 2 · The first fruits
Passover, the sheaf, the fifty days: and Christ the first fruits of the dead.
Point 3 · Nazareth
Familiarity blinds: they took offense, and the Lord could do little for their unbelief.
Take-home line
“Prophets are not without honor except in their own country and in their own house.”
live: Keep holy time (Leviticus 23:4)
Choose one rhythm of holy time and keep it faithfully this week: Sunday Mass without hurry, a short daily prayer at the same hour, or the first Friday devotion.
See him afresh (Matthew 13:57)
At the next Mass, ask the Lord to let you see Jesus as if for the first time, and greet someone you take for granted with fresh attention.
saints: St Peter Chrysologus (c. 380–450)

Born at Imola, Archbishop of Ravenna from about 433 until his death. He was called Chrysologus, “golden word,” because of his short, clear and warm sermons, about 180 of which survive. He taught that prayer, fasting and mercy are one: “Prayer knocks at the door, fasting obtains, mercy receives” (Sermon 43, in substance). Pope Benedict XIII declared him a doctor of the Church in 1729. His memorial, 30 July, is optional.
2027-07-30.prayer: O God, who made Saint Peter Chrysologus an outstanding preacher of your incarnate Word, grant, we pray, that we may always ponder in our hearts the mystery of your salvation, which he so wonderfully expounded, and faithfully express it in the way we live. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord, you come near to us on the appointed days and on the plainest days. Open our eyes, so that we may recognise you in the Mass, in the Word and in our neighbour, and keep us from the unbelief of those who knew you too well to know you. Amen.
altar: Israel's feasts were meetings with God at an appointed time. The Mass is the meeting that Christ himself appointed: “Do this in remembrance of me.” It is not new each day, and that is both its strength and its risk, for we may come to it like the people of Nazareth, who thought they knew all about him. Before Communion the priest holds up the host and says: Behold the Lamb of God. Let us look at him as for the first time. The first fruits of the harvest of the dead is there on the altar, risen and giving himself.

2027-07-31.title: Saint Ignatius of Loyola, Priest
readings: In this year of jubilee you shall return, every one of you, to your property
O God, let all the nations praise you!
Herod sent and had John beheaded in the prison
2027-07-31.alt: Memorial. The weekday readings of Week 17 (Year I) are given; the proper readings of the memorial (1 Corinthians 10:31–11:1; Luke 14:25–33) may be used instead. Psalm verses are given in NRSV numbering. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-07-31.verse: And you shall hallow the fiftieth year and you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you: you shall return, every one of you, to your property and every one of you to your family.
theo: The first reading gives the law of the Jubilee, spoken “on Mount Sinai.” Israel is to count seven weeks of years, “seven times seven years,” forty-nine years, and then, “on the tenth day of the seventh month, on the day of atonement,” the trumpet is to be sounded “throughout all your land.” The fiftieth year is holy: “you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you: you shall return, every one of you, to your property and every one of you to your family.” The land is not to be sown or reaped that year; it rests, and the people eat what the field gives by itself. Property that has been sold or lost returns to the family; those who have fallen into debt are released. In effect the Jubilee is a reset, a time when the poor are given back what they have lost and no family is shut out of the land for ever. There are practical rules as well: in buying and selling, “you shall not cheat one another,” and the price is to reflect the number of harvests before the next Jubilee, “but you shall fear your God; for I am the Lord your God.” The year of Jubilee became, for the prophets, a picture of God's saving freedom. Jesus read from Isaiah in the synagogue at Nazareth: “to proclaim release to the captives... to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor” (Luke 4:18–19). The Church keeps Holy Years of Jubilee, the most recent in 2025. The Psalm is a prayer for the blessing to reach beyond Israel: “May God be gracious to us and bless us and make his face to shine upon us, that your way may be known upon earth, your saving power among all nations.”

The Gospel shows the opposite of liberty: a prophet in prison and a king in bondage to his own pride. Herod Antipas, the ruler of Galilee, hears about Jesus and decides that he must be “John the Baptist; he has been raised from the dead.” The Evangelist then tells why he thinks so. John had been arrested because he had said to Herod: “It is not lawful for you to have her,” meaning Herodias, his brother Philip's wife. Herod “wanted to put him to death,” but he “feared the crowd, because they regarded him as a prophet.” St Mark adds that Herod “feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man,” and “liked to listen to him” (Mark 6:20), though he did not act on what he heard. At his birthday banquet Herodias' daughter dances, and Herod, carried away, promises with an oath to give her whatever she asks. Prompted by her mother she says: “Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter.” The king is “grieved, yet out of regard for his oaths and for the guests” he orders it. What a picture of a man who is a king and a slave: afraid of the crowd, afraid of the guests, afraid of looking weak, and not afraid of killing a righteous man. John, in prison, had the freedom Herod lacked. The scene ends with a detail of great tenderness: John's disciples “took the body and buried it; then they went and told Jesus.” They bring their grief to him. Today the Church remembers St Ignatius of Loyola, a man who knew the power of such a decision. Born in 1491 in the Basque country, a courtier and soldier, Ignatius was wounded by a cannonball at Pamplona in 1521. While he recovered at Loyola he read the lives of Christ and of the saints, and noticed that the thoughts of serving God left him peaceful and joyful, while worldly dreams left him empty. That was the beginning of his conversion and of his teaching on the discernment of spirits. At Manresa he began to write the Spiritual Exercises; he studied in Spain and Paris, and gathered friends, among them St Francis Xavier and St Peter Faber; and the Society of Jesus was approved by Pope Paul III in 1540. Ignatius died in Rome on 31 July 1556 and was canonised in 1622. His watchword was “for the greater glory of God,” in Latin Ad maiorem Dei gloriam, which is St Paul's line in the proper reading: “whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.” The Jesuits have long served India: St Francis Xavier landed at Goa in 1542 and worked among the fishing communities of the coast, and Jesuit schools and colleges are found in every part of the country. The proper Gospel for the memorial is Jesus' call to count the cost: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.” Ignatius knew that real freedom is the freedom to give oneself wholly to God.
outline: Opening
Ask: where in your life do you need to hear the trumpet of the Jubilee: to be released, or to release someone?
Point 1 · The year of liberty
Return to your property and family; no cheating; the Lord's favour proclaimed to the poor.
Point 2 · A king who was a slave
Herod fears the crowd and the guests, and kills a prophet; John in prison is the man at liberty.
Point 3 · For the greater glory of God
St Ignatius: wounded at Pamplona, converted at Loyola, and given wholly to God.
Take-home line
“Whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.”
live: Release someone (Leviticus 25:10)
Forgive a debt, a wrong or a grievance this week, or release someone from an expectation you have placed on them.
Do it for God's glory (1 Corinthians 10:31)
Before each task today, say: for the greater glory of God. Do one ordinary task carefully for that sake alone.
saints: St Ignatius of Loyola (1491–1556)

Basque soldier, wounded at Pamplona in 1521, converted at Loyola, author of the Spiritual Exercises, founder of the Society of Jesus (approved 1540) and its first Superior General. He died in Rome on 31 July 1556 and was canonised on 12 March 1622. His motto: for the greater glory of God. Patron of retreats and of soldiers.
2027-07-31.prayer: O God, who raised up Saint Ignatius of Loyola in your Church to further the greater glory of your name, grant that by his help we may imitate him in fighting the good fight on earth and merit to receive with him a crown in heaven. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray with Ignatius: Take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my understanding and my entire will. Give me only your love and your grace, and I am rich enough. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the trumpet of the Jubilee sounds: “Lift up your hearts.” The Lamb of God takes away the sin of the world, and in Communion we are given liberty to return to our true home. St Ignatius used to say the Mass with great devotion and, in his Exercises, taught the prayer that sums up Christian freedom: Take, Lord, and receive. At the altar we make that prayer our own, giving back to God what he has given, and receiving him who gives himself. All things are offered for the greater glory of God.

quick: Paul tells the Ephesians that they are no longer strangers but members of God's household, built on the apostles with Christ as the cornerstone.
Thomas, absent on Easter evening, demands to see and touch the wounds of the Lord; a week later Jesus offers them, and Thomas confesses: My Lord and my God.
Jesus blesses all who believe without seeing; according to tradition, Thomas brought the faith to India and gave his life for it at Mylapore.
2027-07-03.action: Say Thomas's prayer, “My Lord and my God,” at the elevation of the Host today and tomorrow.
2027-07-03.question: What question about faith am I afraid to bring to Christ, and what would it mean to ask it openly?
catechism: How did the disciples come to believe in the resurrection, and is the risen body of Jesus real?
What does it mean to say that the Church is apostolic?
Why is the name of Jesus the heart of Christian prayer?
kidsaint: St Thomas and the king's palace (a story from the old Acts of Thomas)

A very old story says that a king in India wanted a splendid palace, and gave Thomas a large sum of gold to build it. Thomas was a carpenter and builder, and he said he would start. But when the king came back from a journey, there was no palace! Thomas had given all the gold to the poor. The king was furious. But, the story says, God showed the king that Thomas had been building him a palace in heaven, made of kindness. Nobody knows if every detail is true, but the lesson is clear: what we give to the poor is stored in heaven. Lesson: be generous, and trust the Lord who sends us.
2027-07-03.special: Feast of St Thomas, Apostle. Gloria; no Creed. Kept with greater solemnity in many places in India, the land of the Apostle's tradition. Indian Christian Day (observed by several Christian communities).
term: The Church is called apostolic because she is built on the foundation of the apostles, teaches what they taught, and is sent to the world as they were sent. The successors of the apostles are the bishops, who with the Pope guard and hand on the faith (Catechism 857).

family.explain: One of Jesus' friends, Thomas, was not there when Jesus came to see them after he rose from the dead. The others told him: we have seen the Lord! But Thomas said: I will only believe if I see and touch his wounds. A week later Jesus came again. He said: Peace be with you! Then he said to Thomas: look at my hands. And Thomas said: My Lord and my God! Jesus said: happy are those who believe without seeing. That means us! A very long time ago, Thomas travelled to India, and the Christians of Kerala say he told our country about Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for St Thomas and for the faith of India. We pray for all who find it hard to believe.
family.ask: Ask: “Who first told our family about Jesus? How can we thank God for them?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from a Kerala Catholic family lost his faith during his years in a distant city. He kept it quiet, and kept going to Mass with his mother whenever he came home. One 3 July he went with her on pilgrimage to a church that honours St Thomas. In the crowd he found himself saying, almost as a challenge, the words that Thomas had said: if I could only see. Then, as the Host was lifted up, a different sentence came to him, one he had learned as a child: My Lord and my God. He told a friend long afterwards that nothing seemed to happen, no light, no voice. But he never again felt alone in his doubts. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you showed your wounds to Thomas. Show us your face, and make us your witnesses. My Lord and my God. Amen.
share: Let us also go, that we may die with him (John 11:16). Where in my life do I need Thomas's loyalty?
How can we know the way? (John 14:5). What honest question do I carry to Jesus?
My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). When did I last say these words, and mean them?
pm.resp: Go out to all the world and tell the Good News.
interc: For the Church in India, that she may be faithful to the faith received from the apostle Thomas.
For the Pope and the bishops, successors of the apostles.
For those who struggle with doubt, that they may meet the risen Lord.
For missionaries, catechists and teachers of the faith.
For unity among all the Christians who honour St Thomas.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the apostles and gave us the faith through them. Keep us true to what we have received, and give us the joy of those who believe without seeing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious people; whether they listen or not, they shall know that there has been a prophet among them.
Paul asks three times that the thorn in the flesh be taken away and hears: My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.
In Nazareth the people take offence at Jesus; he can do few miracles because of their unbelief, but he goes on teaching in the villages.
2027-07-04.action: Offer your thorn to God, and thank someone close to you whom you take for granted.
2027-07-04.question: Where in my life have I become too familiar with Jesus to be amazed by him?
catechism: Why does God permit suffering and evil?
What does the hidden life of Jesus in Nazareth teach us?
Who are the brothers and sisters of Jesus?
kidsaint: St Elizabeth of Portugal

Elizabeth was a princess who became a queen. She was very rich, but she loved the poor best. She gave bread to hungry people and built places for sick people and for babies who had no mother. One day her husband the king and her son the prince were going to fight a battle. Elizabeth jumped on her horse and rode between the two armies, and asked them to stop. And they did! She is called the Peacemaker. Lesson: kindness and peace are stronger than swords.
2027-07-04.special: Fourteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Gloria and Creed. St Elizabeth of Portugal omitted.
term: A person called by God to speak his word to his people, often an unwelcome word. The prophets of the Old Testament prepared for Christ, who is the Prophet, Priest and King; and through baptism every Christian shares in this prophetic mission, by living and speaking the truth of the Gospel (Catechism 702–716, 783–786).

family.explain: When Jesus was grown up, he went back to Nazareth, the village where he had lived as a boy. On the Sabbath he taught in the synagogue and people were amazed. But then they said: we know him! He is the carpenter, Mary's son. We know his family. And they would not believe. Jesus was sad. He could only heal a few sick people. But he did not stop. He went on teaching in the other villages. St Paul also had a hard thing he asked God to take away, and God said: my grace is enough for you.
family.intention: We thank Jesus for the ordinary days of his life in Nazareth, and we ask him to bless our daily work and our homes.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family whom we do not thank enough, because they are always there?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kottayam, a young man was ordained a priest, and on the following Sunday he said his first Mass in his home parish. After the Mass the elders of the village gathered round him. One old woman, who had lived across the road from his family for sixty years, held his hands and said, laughing: I saw you stealing mangoes from my tree! The people around laughed. Then she added, more quietly: and now you will hold the Lord in those hands. I am sorry I doubted. The young priest told the story afterwards in a homily. He said: I understood the people of Nazareth. It is not easy to believe in someone you have watched growing up. But I also understood the Lord: he comes to us in the ones we know best. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, carpenter of Nazareth, we welcome you in our homes and in our hearts. Let your grace be sufficient for us. Amen.
share: They shall know that there has been a prophet among them (Ezekiel 2:5). Who has been a prophet for me, and did I listen?
My grace is sufficient for you (2 Corinthians 12:9). What is my thorn, and what has God said to me in it?
He was amazed at their unbelief (Mark 6:6). Where is my faith small, and what would open my heart to him?
pm.resp: Our eyes are fixed on the Lord, pleading for his mercy.
interc: For prophets of our time: for the Pope, the bishops, priests and catechists who speak the word of God, even when it is not welcome.
For the sick and for those who carry a thorn that will not go away.
For families, that they may recognise Christ in one another.
For those who work with their hands, as Jesus did.
For our group, that we may grow in faith and be open to the Lord's surprises.
pm.close: Father, you hide the greatness of your power in weakness. Teach us to receive your Son in the ordinary, to trust your grace, and to speak your word with courage. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God takes a shepherd, Amos, from his flock and sends him to prophesy against the injustice of the northern kingdom; the royal priest tries to silence him.
St Paul blesses God for choosing us in Christ before the foundation of the world, redeeming us by his blood, and sealing us with the Holy Spirit.
Jesus sends the Twelve two by two with authority and little else, to proclaim repentance, cast out demons and anoint the sick.
2027-07-11.action: Ask the Lord what he is sending you to do this week, and do it with someone else.
2027-07-11.question: If the Lord took me from what I am doing today and said: go, prophesy, what would I say?
catechism: What does it mean that the Church is apostolic?
How does Ephesians 1 teach us to pray?
What is poverty of heart, and why does Jesus ask for it?
kidsaint: St Benedict

Benedict was a boy from Nursia in Italy who went to school in Rome. But the city was noisy and full of trouble, so he went to live in a quiet cave and pray. Soon other young men came to join him, and in time he founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote a short Rule for monks. Pope St Gregory the Great tells a story about his childhood: his nurse once broke a clay sieve and wept over it, and little Benedict prayed until the sieve was whole again. Many people who knew him later said that the quiet of his heart was his greatest gift. Lesson: to pray, to work and to love other people is a good way to follow Jesus. His memorial, 11 July, gives way to the Sunday this year.
2027-07-11.special: Fifteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Gloria and Creed. St Benedict omitted. In Kerala the monsoon is at its height: pray for farmers and for those affected by the rains.
term: From the Greek apostolos, one who is sent. The Twelve whom Jesus chose are called the Apostles, and the Church is said to be apostolic because she is built on their foundation, keeps their teaching, and is led by the bishops who succeed them (Catechism 857–860). In a wider sense every baptised person shares in the apostolic mission of the Church.

family.explain: Jesus had twelve special friends, the apostles. One day he sent them out to tell everyone in the villages about God. And he sent them two by two, so that nobody had to be alone. They took only a walking stick and sandals. They did not need bags or money, because God would take care of them, and kind families would give them a place to stay. They told people to be sorry for their sins and to love God, and they healed many people who were sick.
family.intention: We pray for our priests and bishops, who carry on the work of the apostles, and for all who bring the Gospel to others.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we visit together this week as a family, to bring them God's love?”

illus: An illustration

In the monsoon of a recent year a young priest and a catechism teacher from a parish in the hills of Wayanad went together, on foot, with an umbrella and a small bag, to visit a family cut off by a landslide on the road. They had little to give: a few packets of biscuits, a rosary, and a promise to return. The mother of the family, who had not spoken to anyone from the parish for months, made them tea on a wood fire and cried quietly while the teacher read the Gospel of the day. When they left, the priest said to his companion: the Lord sent them two by two because one of us would have turned back at the third stream. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the twelve and sent them out two by two. Call us, send us, and be with us on the road. Amen.
share: I am no prophet, nor a prophet's son; but I am a herdsman (Amos 7:14). What gifts and what weaknesses does the Lord want to use in me, even if I feel unqualified?
He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world (Ephesians 1:4). How would my life look if I believed I was chosen and wanted from before time began?
He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two (Mark 6:7). With whom could I share the mission of the Gospel, and what would we do together?
Take nothing for the journey except a staff (Mark 6:8). What do I carry that weighs me down on the road of discipleship?
pm.resp: Lord, let us see your kindness, and grant us your salvation.
interc: For the Church, that she may be faithful to the apostolic mission and be sent out, poor and joyful, to proclaim repentance and hope.
For Pope Leo XIV, our bishops and priests, that they may be like Amos, fearless in the face of power.
For all who suffer from the monsoon rains, floods and landslides, and for those who help them.
For prophets in our time who speak for the poor and the oppressed, and for journalists and lawyers who tell the truth at a cost.
For our group, that we may know that we are chosen and sent, and may go out two by two.
pm.close: Father, you chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world and send us to announce his Gospel. Seal us with your Spirit and keep us faithful on the way. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses asks God's name; God answers “I am who I am,” and joins his Name to the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
God has seen the misery in Egypt, promises liberation, and warns that Pharaoh will let the people go only when compelled by a mighty hand.
Jesus invites all who are weary and burdened to come to him, and offers his easy yoke: he is gentle and humble in heart.
2027-07-15.action: Say to Jesus tonight what is weighing on you most, and ask him to carry it with you.
2027-07-15.question: Whom do I trust to carry my burdens, and how willingly do I let Jesus take his share?
kidsaint: St Bonaventure

Bonaventure was a little boy in Italy who became very ill. His mother prayed to St Francis, and the boy got better. Many years later, a story says, Francis remembered and said: O buona ventura, good fortune! That is how Bonaventure may have got his name. He grew up to join the Franciscan brothers, became a famous teacher and was made a cardinal. He wrote the story of St Francis and taught that studying is not enough: we must love Jesus with all our hearts.

family.explain: Jesus says: Come to me, all you who are tired and carry heavy loads, and I will give you rest. He is gentle and kind, and he never makes us feel small. A yoke is a wooden bar that two oxen wear on their shoulders so they can pull a plough together. Jesus says: wear my yoke, and I will walk with you! If something is too heavy for you to carry alone, you can give it to Jesus. He will carry it with you.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is tired or worried, and we thank Jesus for walking beside us.
family.ask: Ask: “What is a worry or a heavy thing that each of us can give to Jesus tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A farmer near Palakkad once showed a visitor how two bullocks are yoked for ploughing. One was young and strong, the other old and slow. The visitor asked why the farmer put them together, and the farmer smiled. The young one takes most of the weight, he said, and the old one learns to keep the line straight. Neither of them could do the field alone. The visitor remembered it years later when he read Jesus' words about his yoke, and he thought that this is a picture of how Jesus walks with us: we are the slow one, and he takes most of the weight. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, you are who you are, and you are with us. Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, give us rest. Amen.
share: I am who I am (Exodus 3:14). What does it mean to me that God simply is, always there and always faithful?
I have given heed to you and to what has been done to you (Exodus 3:16). When did I feel that God had seen my trouble?
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me (Matthew 11:29). What would it look like to walk with Jesus in the way I deal with my burdens?
pm.resp: Remember the wonderful works he has done.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be a place of rest for the weary and the burdened.
For the Franciscan family and for all who teach theology and the faith, that learning may lead to love.
For those who carry heavy burdens in secret: illness, debts, a broken family, fear for the future.
For peoples who are oppressed and are crying out for justice and dignity, that God's mighty hand may be seen among them.
For our group, that we may take the yoke of Jesus willingly and learn gentleness from him.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your name to Moses and your heart in your Son. Give rest to the weary and make us gentle and humble in heart, like Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jeremiah condemns the shepherds who scatter the flock, and promises that God will gather it and raise up good shepherds and a righteous Branch of David.
St Paul says that Christ is our peace: he has broken down the dividing wall, made one new humanity of two, and given both access to the Father in one Spirit.
Jesus invites the tired apostles to come away and rest, but when he sees the crowd he has compassion, because they are like sheep without a shepherd, and he begins to teach them.
2027-07-18.action: Set apart one hour for rest with the Lord this week, and pray for your parish priest by name.
2027-07-18.question: Do I know the Shepherd's voice, and am I a shepherd to anyone, in my home, parish or workplace?
catechism: Why is the Church called a flock, and who is her shepherd?
In what sense does the priest act in the person of Christ, the Head and Shepherd?
Why does the Church call Sunday a day of rest, and how should it be kept?
kidsaint: St John Vianney

John Vianney was a farm boy in France who had great trouble with his school lessons, and he wanted very much to become a priest. He tried and tried, and at last he was ordained in 1815. He was sent to a small village called Ars. There he prayed, visited the sick and spent up to sixteen hours a day in the confessional, so many people came to him. He lived very simply and gave his food to the poor. He died in 1859 and is the patron of parish priests. Lesson: a good shepherd gives his time and his heart to every sheep.
2027-07-18.special: Sixteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Gloria and Creed. No memorial is omitted this year. The Sunday of the Good Shepherd in the green season: a good day to pray for priests and vocations. It falls in Karkidakam, the Kerala month of rest and renewal.
term: The word pastor is the Latin for shepherd. In the Church the first Shepherd is Christ himself (John 10:11); the Pope, the bishops and the priests are called pastors because, in union with each other, they care for the flock in his name by teaching the faith, celebrating the sacraments and guiding the people with love. The Bible warns pastors, as Jeremiah does today, not to scatter the flock but to serve it (Catechism 754, 1548–1551; 1 Peter 5:2–4).

family.explain: The apostles came back to Jesus after a long journey and told him everything they had done. Jesus saw that they were tired and said: come with me to a quiet place and rest! They went by boat. But so many people had seen them go that they ran along the shore and got there first! Jesus was not cross. He felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he sat down and taught them many things. Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He looks after us, he knows our names and he never gives up on one of us.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and our bishop, for all teachers and parents, who look after us like shepherds, and for children who have no one to care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we find time to rest and to be quiet as a family? Shall we spend one hour this week without any screens, just together?”

illus: An illustration

A parish priest in a hill parish in Idukki had a habit during the rains. After the evening Mass, when the clouds came low, he would take a torch and an umbrella and walk up the path to the houses of the old and the sick, to check that the roofs were holding and that there were candles and rice. Someone once asked him whether he was afraid of the landslides. He said: if I am afraid, I will not go; but if the sheep are afraid, I must go. When the parish was asked years later what they remembered most about him, nobody mentioned his homilies. They said: the torch on the path. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you who see the crowds and have compassion, gather us and lead us. Amen.
share: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want (Psalm 23:1). When did I most feel that the Lord was leading me, and in what way?
For he is our peace (Ephesians 2:14). Where is there a wall between me and someone else, and what is one small step I can take to take it down?
Come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while (Mark 6:31). How do I make room for rest and quiet in my week, and how does it help me serve?
pm.resp: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
interc: For Pope Leo XIV, our bishop and all priests, that they may be shepherds after the heart of Christ and lose no sheep.
For young people who are discerning a call to the priesthood and religious life, that they may have courage to say yes.
For all who are tired, overworked or burnt out, in ministry and in families, that they may find rest.
For peace between peoples, castes and religions, and for the walls of hostility to come down.
For our group, that we may know the Shepherd's voice and follow him together.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the Good Shepherd and as our peace. Gather your scattered flock, raise up faithful shepherds and make us one in your Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Elisha feeds a hundred people with twenty barley loaves, because the Lord says: They shall eat and have some left.
St Paul begs the Ephesians to keep the unity of the Spirit: one body, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all.
Jesus takes a boy's five barley loaves and two fish, gives thanks, and feeds about five thousand, and nothing is lost.
catechism: How does the miracle of the loaves point to the Eucharist?
How does the Eucharist make the Church one?
What do we ask for when we pray: Give us this day our daily bread?
kidsaint: St James the Apostle

James was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee with his brother John, and Jesus called them both from their father's boat. Jesus nicknamed them the Sons of Thunder, because they were quick to anger and quick to love. James was with Jesus on the mountain of the Transfiguration and in the garden of Gethsemane. He was the first of the Twelve to give his life for Jesus. People say that his body rests in a great church in Spain, and pilgrims still walk hundreds of miles to pray there. Lesson: a hot temper can become a great love when it is given to Jesus.
2027-07-25.special: Seventeenth Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). Gloria and Creed. John 6, the Bread of Life, begins. St James the Apostle omitted. World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly.
term: From the Greek eucharistia, “thanksgiving.” The Mass is the Eucharist because Jesus gave thanks over the bread and wine, and because in it the Church gives thanks to the Father for all his gifts. The bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ, truly, really and substantially present, and the Mass makes present his one sacrifice on the Cross (Catechism 1328–1332, 1374). It is called Holy Communion because it unites us to Christ and to one another.

family.explain: A big crowd followed Jesus, and it was getting late. Everyone was hungry. Jesus asked his friends: how can we feed all these people? Then a boy came forward with five little loaves and two small fish. It was not much. But Jesus said thank you to God for it, broke the bread, and gave it out, and everybody ate until they were full! There were twelve baskets left over. When we give Jesus the little we have, he can do wonders.
family.intention: We pray for people who are hungry and for those who share their food. We thank God for our grandparents and pray for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us give this week? Which grandparent or old neighbour shall we visit or call?”

illus: An illustration

In the lean month of Karkidakam, when the rains kept the boats ashore and the shop credit ran out, a parish on the Kerala coast opened its hall every noon to anyone who was hungry. On the first day the cooks had rice for forty. A fisherman's widow came in with a small bag of her own rice and said: it is not much. The next day others came, with a bag of rice, a handful of dal, a few coconuts. Within a week the parish was feeding over two hundred people every noon. The priest said that he never understood how it was done; he only knew that the pot never emptied before everyone had eaten, and that the widow's little bag had been the beginning. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you took the loaves and gave thanks. Take what we bring, bless it and make us one. Amen.
share: Twenty loaves, a hundred people (2 Kings 4:43). Where do I see only the arithmetic, and not the word of the Lord?
Five barley loaves and two fish: but what are they among so many people? (John 6:9). What small thing have I been keeping back because it seems too little?
One bread, one body (1 Corinthians 10:17). What would I need to do to keep the unity of the Spirit in my family and in my parish?
pm.resp: The hand of the Lord feeds us; he answers all our needs.
interc: For the Church, that she may feed the world with the Word of God and the Bread of Life and keep the unity of the Spirit.
For Pope Leo XIV, our bishops and priests, who take, bless, break and give in the name of Christ.
For all who are hungry in this lean season of the monsoon, and for those who share their bread with them.
For grandparents and the elderly, on this World Day, that they may be honoured, visited and cared for, and that the young may receive the faith they hand on.
For our group, that we may offer our five loaves and trust that the Lord will make them enough.
pm.close: Father, you feed us with your Word and with the Body and Blood of your Son. Make us one body, and send us to feed the hungry. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God tests Abraham: he is to offer Isaac, the son of the promise; Abraham obeys in faith, and God provides a ram in his place.
The Lord swears an oath to Abraham: his descendants will be as many as the stars, and in his offspring all nations will be blessed.
Jesus sees the faith of the friends, forgives the paralysed man and heals him, to show that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.
2027-07-01.action: Carry one person in prayer today, and make a firm plan to go to confession this month.
2027-07-01.question: When God asks something I do not understand, do I say with Abraham, “Here I am,” and leave the lamb to him?

family.explain: Abraham loved his son Isaac very much. One day God asked Abraham to trust him in a very hard way. Abraham got up early, took wood, and walked up a mountain with Isaac. Isaac asked: where is the lamb? Abraham said: God himself will provide the lamb. And at the last moment God stopped Abraham and gave him a ram. God never wants a child to be hurt. He keeps his promises, and he provides. In the Gospel, some friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus, and Jesus made him well.
family.intention: We thank God for those who carry us when we are weak. We pray for the sick, and for children who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Who has carried us when things were hard? Whom can we help carry this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill parish of Idukki, the monsoon had swollen the stream that separated one hamlet from the chapel. An old man who had been paralysed for years had said he would like to receive the Anointing of the Sick before he died. Four young men of the village made a cot out of two bamboo poles and a bedsheet, waded the stream chest-deep and carried him across, with the rain beating on their shoulders. The priest, who told the story afterwards, said the old man said little. He only kept repeating: they carried me. The priest thought of the roof in the Gospel and of the words, When Jesus saw their faith. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Abraham, you provide what we need. Lord Jesus, forgive us and carry us to the Father. Amen.
share: God himself will provide the lamb (Genesis 22:8). Where in my life am I afraid that God will not provide?
Abraham said, “Here I am” (Genesis 22:1, 11). Do I say these words to God each morning?
When Jesus saw their faith (Matthew 9:2). Whose faith carried me, and whom can I carry?
pm.resp: Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give glory.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of forgiveness and healing.
For priests who hear confessions, and for those who have been away from the sacrament for a long time.
For people with paralysis, for their families and for those who care for them.
For parents who must trust God with a child they cannot protect.
For our group, that we may learn to carry one another.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Son for us, and in him you forgive us. Keep us in your covenant and make us trusting servants of your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sarah dies at Hebron; Abraham mourns her, and buys a cave at Machpelah from the Hittites as a tomb.
Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac among his kin; Isaac meets Rebekah, loves her and is comforted after his mother's death.
Jesus calls Matthew, the tax collector, eats with sinners, and says that he has come to call not the righteous but sinners.
2027-07-02.action: Pray for your dead today, and invite someone who is alone to share a meal.
2027-07-02.question: Do I come to Jesus as one of the sick who need a physician, or as one of the well who need nothing?
kidsaint: St Margaret Mary Alacoque

Margaret Mary was a French girl who was often ill. When she grew up she became a sister at a convent in Paray-le-Monial. One day, while she was praying in front of the Blessed Sacrament, Jesus showed her his heart, full of love for everyone. He asked her to tell people to love his Sacred Heart and to receive Communion on the First Fridays. Some people did not believe Margaret Mary at first. But her friend, a Jesuit priest called Claude de la Colombière, believed her and helped. Now many people all over the world love the Sacred Heart. Lesson: Jesus loves us with a real heart, and he wants us to love him back.

family.explain: Matthew was a tax collector. Nobody liked tax collectors, because they took people's money. One day Jesus walked by and said to Matthew: follow me. And Matthew stood up and followed! Then Matthew had a big dinner at his house, and Jesus sat down to eat with his friends, even those whom others called sinners. The teachers were cross about this. But Jesus said: I came for those who need me, like a doctor for the sick.
family.intention: We thank Jesus for loving everybody. We pray for those who feel left out, and for all the people in our family who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or in our street who is always left out? How can we sit with them this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Thrissur, a retired bank manager had a name for strictness. Customers feared him, and so did some of his own family. After a heart attack he began to come to the First Friday evening Mass, sitting at the back. A year later nobody remembered exactly when it began, but the parish noticed that the school fees of some children were being paid quietly, and the sick were being driven to the hospital. He did not like to be thanked. When the priest asked him what had happened, the old man said: a doctor told me I was ill in my body. The Lord told me I was ill in my heart. I had come to the right clinic. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Abraham, you comfort those who mourn. Lord Jesus, you called Matthew and still eat with sinners. Sacred Heart of Jesus, we trust in you. Amen.
share: I am a stranger and an alien (Genesis 23:4). What helps me remember that this world is not my final home?
He loved her. So Isaac was comforted (Genesis 24:67). Who has comforted me in a time of sorrow, and whom can I comfort?
He got up and followed him (Matthew 9:9). What am I sitting at that I must leave to follow Jesus?
pm.resp: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good.
interc: For those who mourn, and for the souls of the faithful departed.
For husbands and wives, that their love may be a sign of God's faithfulness.
For those who feel despised or excluded, as Matthew was.
For priests who offer Mass and hear confessions on First Fridays.
For our group, that we may desire mercy more than sacrifice.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to call sinners. Give us the Heart of Jesus, merciful and humble, that we may follow him all our days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jacob flees from Esau, sleeps on a stone and dreams of a ladder to heaven; the Lord promises to be with him wherever he goes.
Jacob wakes and says: Surely the Lord is in this place; he sets up the stone as a pillar and calls the place Bethel.
A synagogue leader asks Jesus to raise his dead daughter; on the way a woman is healed by touching his cloak; Jesus takes the girl by the hand and she rises.
2027-07-05.action: Say Surely the Lord is in this place, quietly, three times today.
2027-07-05.question: Where in my ordinary life could God be present, and I did not know it?
kidsaint: St Anthony Zaccaria

Anthony was a boy in Italy whose father died when he was little, and his mother taught him to love the poor. He became a doctor, because he wanted to help sick people. But he saw that many people were sick in a different way: they had forgotten God. So he became a priest, and with his friends he started a group called the Barnabites. They went through towns talking about Jesus and taking care of people. Anthony loved to read the letters of St Paul. He died when he was only thirty-six. Lesson: we can help people's bodies and hearts, and we can lead them to Jesus.

family.explain: Jacob was alone and afraid. He lay down on the ground with a stone as his pillow and fell asleep. In his dream he saw a ladder going up to heaven, and angels climbing up and down. God said: I am with you. When Jacob woke up, he said: surely God is in this place, and I did not know it! In the Gospel, a woman touched the edge of Jesus' cloak and was healed, and Jesus took a little girl by the hand and she got up.
family.intention: We thank God that he is with us wherever we are, at home, at school, on the road. We pray for children who are frightened or far from home.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we afraid, and God was with us?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a village in Pathanamthitta left for work in the Gulf, and spent his first night in a crowded labour camp, with his bag under his head. He had never been so far from his mother. She had pressed a small crucifix into his hand at the airport. In the middle of the night, hearing the snoring of forty strangers and the roar of the air-conditioner, he took the crucifix out, held it and said, almost without thinking: Lord, you are in this place too. He told his parish priest, years later, that he did not feel an angel, only that he fell asleep at once. And that when he woke, the camp looked different: not a prison, but a place where he could pray. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Jacob, you are with us wherever we go. Lord Jesus, we touch the fringe of your cloak with faith. Amen.
share: I did not know it! (Genesis 28:16). Where has God been present in my life without my knowing?
I am with you and will keep you wherever you go (Genesis 28:15). What fear does this promise answer?
If I only touch his cloak (Matthew 9:21). What do I bring to Jesus with the faith of this woman?
pm.resp: My God, in whom I trust.
interc: For those who are far from home, migrant workers, students and refugees.
For the sick who touch the Lord's cloak in faith through prayer and the sacraments.
For doctors, nurses and all who heal.
For priests and religious in the spirit of St Anthony Zaccaria.
For our group, that we may see God in ordinary places.
pm.close: Father, you are in this place and in every place. Keep us in your promise and bring us home. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jacob wrestles with a stranger at the Jabbok until daybreak, receives the name Israel, a blessing and a limp.
Jacob names the place Peniel: he has seen God face to face and lives.
Jesus heals a mute man, has compassion on the crowds like sheep without a shepherd, and asks his disciples to pray for labourers for the harvest.
2027-07-06.action: Pray ten minutes today without giving up, and say one Hail Mary for vocations.
2027-07-06.question: Do I hold on to the Lord in prayer until he blesses me, or do I give up when he does not answer quickly?
kidsaint: St Maria Goretti

Maria lived in a small house in Italy. Her family was poor, her father died, and Maria helped her mother with cooking, cleaning and caring for the little ones. She loved Jesus very much and prayed every day. She made her First Communion when she was eleven. One day a young man who lived nearby tried to make her do something bad. Maria said: no, it is a sin! God does not want it! The young man hurt her badly, and she died the next day. Before she died, she said she forgave him. Years later he said sorry and became a good man. Lesson: say no to sin, and forgive those who hurt you.

family.explain: Jacob was alone by a river at night when a stranger wrestled with him until morning. Jacob would not let go. He said: bless me! And the stranger gave him a new name, Israel, and blessed him. Jacob said: I have seen God face to face! In the Gospel, Jesus looked at big crowds and felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. He said: the harvest is big, but there are few workers. Let us pray that God sends more workers!
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters, brothers and teachers of the faith, and for children who may be called to serve God.
family.ask: Ask: “What would it mean for us to ask God again and again for something, without giving up?”

illus: An illustration

A woman of a coastal parish near Kollam had prayed for twelve years for her husband, who had stopped going to church after a loss in business. Each evening she prayed the rosary at the foot of a small crucifix, saying to the Lord quietly: I will not let you go until you bless him. Her friends told her to stop; the husband laughed at her. But one morning he came down to the kitchen and said: take me to Mass. He never said what had changed. Only that he had heard her through the wall the night before, speaking to the Lord as if wrestling with him, and that he did not want her to wrestle alone. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Jacob, we do not let go of you. Lord of the harvest, send labourers into your harvest. Amen.
share: I will not let you go, unless you bless me (Genesis 32:26). What blessing am I asking for, and how long have I been asking?
He had compassion for them (Matthew 9:36). Whom do I see as harassed and helpless?
Ask the Lord of the harvest (Matthew 9:38). How could I help a young person to listen to God's call?
pm.resp: I shall behold your face in righteousness.
interc: For those who struggle in prayer, that they may not give up.
For vocations to the priesthood, the religious life and lay missions.
For young people, that they may follow St Maria Goretti's love of purity.
For victims of violence, and for the grace of forgiveness for those who have been hurt.
For our group, that we may hold on to the Lord in faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave Jacob the name Israel after a night of struggle. Give us perseverance in prayer and zeal for your harvest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Famine spreads, and Pharaoh sends the people to Joseph; Joseph's brothers come to Egypt and bow before him without recognising him.
Joseph tests his brothers; they confess to one another that they are paying for what they did to him, and he weeps in secret.
Jesus calls the Twelve, names them, gives them authority and sends them first to the lost sheep of Israel with the message: the kingdom has come near.
2027-07-07.action: Choose one wrong from the past that you have never put right, and take a first step this week.
2027-07-07.question: When my conscience speaks, do I silence it, or do I let it lead me home?

family.explain: Jesus had many followers, but he chose twelve special friends and gave each of them a name and a task. He sent them to tell everyone: God is very near! Long before, Joseph had ten brothers who were unkind to him. Years later, when they were hungry, they came to him for food. He did not shout at them. He wanted to see if they were sorry now. Being sorry is the first step to being a family again.
family.intention: We pray for families that are hurt by quarrels, for hungry people everywhere, and for our priests and bishops, who carry on the work of the Twelve.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family I need to say sorry to, or someone who is waiting to hear sorry from me?”

illus: An illustration

A retired farmer from the hill country of Idukki once told his parish priest that he had not slept properly since the first rains of the monsoon. Forty years earlier, in a very bad year for pepper and paddy, he had quietly taken some sacks of rice from his elder brother's store, and he had never said a word. The priest did not ask for details; he said only: go to your brother. The old man went, trembling, with a bag of rice on his shoulder. His brother met him at the gate, looked at the bag, and began to weep. I knew in the first year, he said, and I forgave you before the next harvest. I was only waiting for you to come. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you bring good out of famine and tears. Lord Jesus, you call us by name and send us. Give us your Spirit as we read your word. Amen.
share: Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do (Genesis 41:55). Whom do I go to when I am in need, and whom does God want me to obey?
We are paying the penalty for what we did to our brother (Genesis 42:21). What does my conscience bring up from the past, and what would it mean to put it right?
He turned away from them and wept (Genesis 42:24). When have I seen love hidden behind a hard face, in my family or in God's dealings with me?
The kingdom of heaven has come near (Matthew 10:7). What would it look like in my street or workplace if I believed this and said it?
pm.resp: Truly the eye of the Lord is on those who fear him.
interc: For the Church, that she may bring the word and the bread of Christ to all who hunger, as the apostles did.
For all who suffer hunger and famine, and for those who work to feed them.
For families divided by old wrongs, that they may find the courage to say sorry and to forgive.
For our bishops and priests, successors and helpers of the Twelve, that they may be faithful and humble.
For our group, that we may hear the word of Jesus and go where he sends us.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to gather the lost sheep and you send us in his name. Heal our divisions and make us messengers of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Judah offers himself as a slave in place of Benjamin; Joseph reveals himself: I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt; God sent me before you to preserve life.
Psalm 105 retells it: Joseph, sold as a slave, tested by the word of the Lord, was sent ahead of his family to save them.
Jesus sends the Twelve to heal and to proclaim, with no money and no bag: You received without payment; give without payment.
2027-07-08.action: Do one good thing today for which you expect nothing at all in return.
2027-07-08.question: Can I say with Joseph that God has brought good out of the wrong done to me, and forgive as he forgave?

family.explain: Joseph's brothers had been very unkind to him. Now he was a powerful man in Egypt, and they stood in front of him, afraid. He could have punished them. Instead he cried and said: I am Joseph, your brother! Come closer. Do not be sad. God sent me here to save our family. Jesus tells his friends: you got God's love as a gift, so give it as a gift too. When we forgive without asking for anything, we are like Joseph and like Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the people who have hurt us, and for the people we have hurt, that we may forgive and be forgiven.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift have we received from God this week? Whom can we share it with, without asking for anything back?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in the hills above Munnar once received a young priest who had no money for a car and walked from one chapel to the next, carrying a small bag with a Bible, a stole and the oils. In the tea estates the families welcomed him without being asked, and he stayed in line houses, in a classroom, once in a cow shed during a landslide warning. He never charged for a blessing or a Mass. At the end of his first year the families, who had very little, quietly collected enough to buy him a pair of strong boots. He told the bishop it was the best gift he had ever received. I gave what I was given, he said, and they gave me back more. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you are the God who sent Joseph ahead of his family to save them. Lord Jesus, you give without payment. Teach us to receive and to give. Amen.
share: Let your servant remain as a slave to my lord in place of the boy (Genesis 44:33). When have I offered myself for someone else, and what did it cost?
I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt (Genesis 45:4). What is it like to be forgiven by someone whom I have wronged?
God sent me before you to preserve life (Genesis 45:5). Where can I see God's hand in a hurt that I have suffered?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What have I received from God that I have never thought of passing on?
pm.resp: He had sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
interc: For the Church, that she may give healing and the word of God without payment, and live in trust and simplicity.
For those who have been betrayed by their own family, that they may find healing and perhaps reconciliation.
For priests and missionaries who travel light and depend on the welcome of ordinary homes.
For all who offer themselves in the place of others: parents, nurses, carers, soldiers and volunteers.
For our group, that we may receive without payment and give without payment.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Son for us without payment and sent him to bring us home. Teach us to forgive as Joseph forgave and to give as Christ gave. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God appears to Jacob at Beer-sheba and promises: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also bring you up again; Jacob and Joseph meet in Goshen with tears.
Psalm 37 sings the trust of the righteous, who have abundance even in famine, and whose salvation is from the Lord.
Jesus warns the Twelve that they go out like sheep among wolves, and promises that the Spirit of the Father will speak through them.
2027-07-09.action: Pray today by name for one Christian community that lives under pressure.
2027-07-09.question: Do I go into hard places with the confidence that God goes down with me?

family.explain: Old Jacob had to leave his home and go to a new country, and he was afraid. In the night God called him: Jacob, Jacob! And God said: do not be afraid. I will go with you. And God kept his promise. When Jacob saw Joseph again, he was so happy that he said: now I can die in peace! Jesus told his friends that it would not always be easy to follow him, but that the Holy Spirit would give them the words to say. Many brave Christians have died for Jesus. We call them martyrs.
family.intention: We pray for children and families who have to leave their homes, and for Christians who are in danger because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When was the last time we were frightened about something new? How can we remember that God goes with us?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman from a coastal village near Kochi once left for her first job in the Gulf, leaving behind a mother who had never been outside her district. At the airport her mother gave her a small card with a line from the Bible written in pencil: I myself will go down with you. The girl spent the first months in a crowded hostel, homesick and afraid. On the worst night she took out the card and read the line aloud, and she said it felt as though her mother's voice and God's voice were saying the same thing. Years later she put the same card into the hand of her own daughter on her first day at college. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Jacob, you go down with us into every foreign land. Lord Jesus, you promise us the Spirit when we are afraid. Be with us. Amen.
share: Jacob, Jacob. Here I am (Genesis 46:2). When has God called me by name, and how did I answer?
I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also bring you up again (Genesis 46:4). Where do I most need to hear this promise in my own life?
I can die now, having seen for myself that you are still alive (Genesis 46:30). What would it take for me to be at peace in this way?
I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). Where am I asked to be wise as a serpent and innocent as a dove?
pm.resp: The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord.
interc: For the Church in China and in every land where Christians are persecuted or restricted, that they may keep faith and hope.
For the martyrs of every age, St Augustine Zhao Rong and his companions, and St Devasahayam, that their witness may strengthen us.
For migrants and families who travel far from home, that they may know that God travels with them.
For elderly parents waiting to see their children again, that they may be given the gift of that meeting.
For our group, that the Spirit of the Father may speak through us when we are called to give an answer.
pm.close: Father, you go with your people into every land and you give your Spirit to those who witness to you. Keep us faithful to the end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jacob dies and is carried to Machpelah; the brothers fear that Joseph will take revenge, and Joseph answers: Do not be afraid! Am I in the place of God? God intended it for good.
Joseph dies in Egypt after making the Israelites swear to carry up his bones when God comes to them, and Genesis ends with a coffin and a promise.
Jesus tells his disciples three times not to be afraid: the truth will come out, the Father cares for the sparrows, and he acknowledges those who acknowledge him.
2027-07-10.action: Hand over to God one fear you have been carrying for a long time.
2027-07-10.question: Do I still fear people whom God has already helped me to forgive, or who have already forgiven me?

family.explain: After their father died, Joseph's brothers were afraid again. They thought: now Joseph will punish us. But Joseph cried and said: do not be afraid! I am not in the place of God. You meant to hurt me, but God turned it into good. I will look after you and your children. Jesus says something like that to us.
