God cares for even the tiniest sparrow, and he has counted every hair on your head. So do not be afraid: you are more precious to him than many sparrows!
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid or worried, and for those who have said sorry and are waiting to be forgiven.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we afraid of as a family? How can we hand it to God together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

After a funeral Mass in a parish near Thrissur, a man took the village priest aside and asked in a low voice whether his elder brother, with whom he had been in dispute for years over a piece of paddy land, would now take him to court, since their father was no longer there to keep the peace. The priest said: why not go and ask him? The younger brother went to the house with fear in his stomach. His elder brother met him in the yard, put a hand on his shoulder and said: our father asked only that the two of us would still be sitting at one table when he was gone. Come and eat. It had never occurred to him to punish anyone. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of Joseph, you turn evil into good. Lord Jesus, you tell us not to be afraid. Take our fears into your hands. Amen.
share: Do not be afraid! Am I in the place of God? (Genesis 50:19). Where am I tempted to take God's place in judging someone?
God intended it for good (Genesis 50:20). What evil in my life has God already begun to turn into good?
God will surely come to you (Genesis 50:24). What promise of God am I carrying, even when I cannot see its fulfilment?
So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:31). What fear can I hand to the Father who numbers the hairs of my head?
pm.resp: Seek the Lord and his strength; seek his presence continually.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim in the light what Jesus has told her in the dark, without fear.
For those who live in fear: of illness, of debt, of violence, of the future.
For reconciliation between brothers and sisters divided by property, money or old injuries.
For the dying, that they may receive the Lord as food for the journey, and for those who sit beside them.
For our group, that we may seek the Lord and his strength, and his presence continually.
pm.close: Father, you know every sparrow and every hair of our heads. Take away our fear and make us witnesses to your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A new king who does not know Joseph fears the Israelites, makes them slaves and orders that every Hebrew boy be thrown into the Nile; but the more they are oppressed, the more they multiply.
Psalm 124 gives thanks that the Lord was on Israel's side and that the snare is broken: our help is in the name of the Lord.
Jesus says he brings not peace but a sword that divides, asks to be loved above everything, and promises a reward even for a cup of cold water given in his name.
2027-07-12.action: Give a cup of cold water, in some form, to someone who needs it today.
2027-07-12.question: Is there anyone I have stopped thanking, or anyone I have begun to fear, because of what I have forgotten?

family.explain: A long time after Joseph had died, a new king ruled Egypt who did not remember the good Joseph had done. He was afraid of the Israelites, and he made them work very hard as slaves. But God was with them, and they became even stronger. Two brave women, Shiphrah and Puah, would not obey the king when he told them to hurt the babies. They obeyed God. Jesus says that every kind thing we do for others, even giving a cup of cold water, is seen by God and will never be lost.
family.intention: We pray for children and workers who are made to work too hard, and for everyone who is afraid of strangers.
family.ask: Ask: “Who has helped our family in the past, so that we may thank them? And who needs a cup of water from us today?”

illus: An illustration

At a brick kiln near a town in Kerala, a priest on a Sunday visit met a group of migrant workers who had come from another state to work there during the dry months. They lived in huts by the kiln and had been told that the weekly day of rest was a luxury. The priest asked for nothing except to sit with them; a woman from the parish had sent a large flask of tea and some banana chips. A young man who had not been home for nine months said afterwards that he could not remember the last time someone had asked his name. The woman from the parish was invited to the kiln the next week, and she went, not alone, but with her children. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you saw the misery of your people and came down to deliver them. Lord Jesus, you tell us to welcome one another in your name. Be with us. Amen.
share: A new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph (Exodus 1:8). What good done to me by others have I forgotten, and who might need my gratitude?
The more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied (Exodus 1:12). Where have I seen God's life grow in the face of hardship?
The midwives feared God (Exodus 1:17). When have I been asked to do something wrong, and what helped me to refuse?
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me (Matthew 10:37). What is the one thing I find hardest to put second to Christ?
Whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones (Matthew 10:42). Who is a little one who needs a welcome from me?
pm.resp: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
interc: For the Church, that she may never forget the poor, and may be a home for refugees, migrants and workers who are not welcome elsewhere.
For all who suffer forced labour, trafficking and slavery in our own time, and for those who work to bring them release.
For those who refuse to carry out unjust orders at a cost to themselves, and for midwives, doctors and nurses who protect life.
For families divided by faith, that they may find peace and respect without betraying Christ.
For our group, that we may be quick to give a cup of cold water in his name.
pm.close: Father, you hear the cry of the oppressed and you are our help. Teach us to welcome others as we welcome you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A mother hides her baby, then places him in a basket on the Nile; the daughter of Pharaoh takes pity on him and names him Moses, “drawn out.”
Moses, grown up, defends a kinsman, kills an Egyptian, is rejected by his own people and flees to Midian.
Jesus grieves over Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, which saw most of his deeds of power and did not repent.
2027-07-13.action: Thank, by name or by letter or call, one person who held you up when you could not hold yourself.
2027-07-13.question: Do I treat the gifts of my faith as a treasure to use or only as something I already have?
kidsaint: St Henry

Henry lived a thousand years ago in Germany and became a king and then an emperor. He did not want to be a king for his own glory. He wanted to look after poor people and to keep peace. He built churches and helped build a new diocese at a city called Bamberg. He prayed a great deal. His wife, Kunigunde, was a saint too. Henry teaches us that being strong means helping others.

family.explain: A mother loved her baby very much, but a bad king wanted to harm baby boys. She made a little basket, put her baby inside and placed it among the reeds at the river's edge. His big sister watched from far away. The king's daughter came to wash in the river, found the baby and felt sorry for him. She gave him a name: Moses, which means “drawn out of the water.” God was looking after him all the time, and when he grew up he led God's people to safety.
family.intention: We thank God for our parents, grandparents and everyone who has looked after us, and we pray for children who have no one to look after them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who helped to look after me when I was small? How can I say thank you this week?”

illus: An illustration

In the floods of 2018 a young nurse near the Pamba river spent two nights on a rooftop with strangers. A fisherman's boat reached them and took her to a relief camp, and in the camp a stranger shared her only dry blanket with her. Years later the nurse could not recall the fisherman's name, but she could recall the blanket exactly. She said she now keeps one spare blanket in her car for anyone who needs it. We are all people who were once pulled out of the water by someone whose name we may not remember; and one day we will be asked whom we pulled out. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you hear the groaning of your people. Draw us out of the water, and make us grateful. Amen.
share: She put the child in it and placed it among the reeds (Exodus 2:3). Who placed me safely and watched from a distance when I was small or weak?
Who made you a ruler and judge over us? (Exodus 2:14). Has God ever sent me to help someone who did not welcome me, and how did I respond?
Woe to you, Chorazin! (Matthew 11:21). Which of the gifts God has given me have I begun to take for granted?
pm.resp: You who seek God, let your hearts revive.
interc: For the Church, that she may grieve over the world's sins with the heart of Jesus and not with anger.
For all who care for children who have been abandoned, and for those who adopt them.
For rulers and public servants, that like St Henry they may see power as a duty to the poor.
For victims of floods and the monsoon rains, and for those who rescue them.
For our group, that we may turn back to the Lord quickly and gratefully.
pm.close: Father, you drew Moses out of the water and sent him to deliver your people. Draw us to yourself, and let our lives be thanks for all that we have received. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses, a shepherd in Midian, turns aside to look at a bush that burns and is not consumed; God calls him by name and tells him to remove his sandals.
God says: I have seen my people's misery and heard their cry; I will send you, and I will be with you.
Jesus thanks the Father for revealing his secrets to infants and speaks of the knowledge between the Father and the Son.
2027-07-14.action: Visit, call or pray for someone who is ill today, and treat the moment as holy ground.
2027-07-14.question: When did I last stop, turn aside and make room for God to speak?
kidsaint: St Camillus de Lellis

Camillus was tall and strong, and when he was young he was a soldier. One day he hurt his leg badly, and the wound would not heal. He went to a hospital in Rome, and there he saw how lonely and uncared for the sick were. He decided to spend his life nursing them. He started a group of brothers, called the Camillians, who wear a red cross, and he is said to have told them: put more heart into those hands. When you help someone who is ill, you help Jesus.

family.explain: Moses was looking after sheep when he saw something strange: a bush on fire that did not burn up! He went closer to look, and God called his name: Moses, Moses! God said: take off your sandals, because this is holy ground. God told Moses that he had seen how his people were suffering and that he would send Moses to help them. Moses was afraid, but God said: I will be with you. God is always with us, too, especially when we are helping someone who is hurting.
family.intention: We pray for sick people, for doctors and nurses, and for all who look after them. We thank God that he is always with us.
family.ask: Ask: “Who do we know who is sick? What could we make or bring, or what could we say, to cheer them up this week?”

illus: An illustration

A senior nurse in a government hospital in Kerala trained her new nurses with one rule. When you enter a ward, she told them, say good morning to the patient before you look at the chart. The patient is not a case, she said; the patient is a person standing on holy ground. A young nurse later said that she did not understand the rule until a frightened old man in the bed grasped her hand and said: thank you for seeing me. The nurse added that she never forgot that the chart can wait for ten seconds. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you who see the sufferings of your people, turn us aside to see what you show us, and take away our fear. Amen.
share: I must turn aside and look at this great sight (Exodus 3:3). What would help me to stop and notice God in my day?
Remove the sandals from your feet (Exodus 3:5). Where do I need to approach God, or my neighbour, with more reverence?
You have hidden these things from the wise and revealed them to infants (Matthew 11:25). In what ways has God taught me through the humble and the little?
pm.resp: The Lord works vindication and justice for all who are oppressed.
interc: For all who are sick, especially the dying, that they may know the nearness of Christ.
For doctors, nurses, chaplains and caregivers, that they may serve with St Camillus' tenderness.
For those who suffer in silence and whom no one visits.
For the Church, that she may always be a place of welcome for the little and the poor.
For our group, that we may turn aside, listen and answer: Here I am.
pm.close: Father, you saw the misery of your people and sent Moses to deliver them. Send us to all who suffer, and be with us as you promised. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On the night of the Passover each family takes an unblemished lamb, marks the doorposts with its blood and eats it in haste; God passes over their homes.
The disciples pluck grain on the sabbath; Jesus replies that something greater than the temple is here, that God desires mercy, and that he is lord of the sabbath.
On Mount Carmel Elijah prays seven times and sees a little cloud rising from the sea; Mary, Our Lady of Mount Carmel, is the one who bore the rain of grace.
2027-07-16.action: Pray one Hail Mary for a need that is still unanswered, and add: Mother, help me to wait like Elijah.
2027-07-16.question: Do I keep going back to prayer, like Elijah's servant who looked seven times, or do I stop after the first “There is nothing”?
kidsaint: Our Lady of Mount Carmel

A long time ago, on a mountain by the sea called Mount Carmel, a prophet named Elijah prayed for rain. He sent his helper to look at the sky, and the helper came back six times: nothing! The seventh time he said: I see a tiny cloud, as small as a man's hand! Soon the rain came. Many centuries later, Christian hermits lived on the same mountain and built a little chapel for Mary. They are called the Carmelites. Some people wear a small brown cloth, called a scapular, to remember that Mary loves them and that they want to follow her.

family.explain: Elijah was praying for rain. There had been no rain for a long time and everything was dry. He told his helper: look at the sea! Six times the helper said: nothing! But Elijah did not give up. The seventh time the helper saw a small cloud, no bigger than a hand. Soon the sky was dark and the rain came pouring down. Mary is like that little cloud: small and humble, but she brought Jesus to us. And Jesus is the one who gives us everything we need.
family.intention: We pray for rain where it is needed, and where there is too much rain, and for all farmers and fishermen. We thank Mary for being our mother, and ask her to help us to do whatever Jesus tells us.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we waiting for? Shall we pray for it every day this week, like Elijah, and not give up?” Say a Hail Mary together.

illus: An illustration

A woman in a coastal village near Kollam used to sit on her veranda every evening from the first week of June, looking at the sky. Her husband was a fisherman and the sea was rough. She told her granddaughter once that when the sky looks empty, she says her rosary and looks for the first little cloud, and that Our Lady, who knows what it is to wait and to hope, always sends one. One evening the girl saw a cloud no bigger than her own hand, and the old woman smiled and said: that is the beginning. Soon the rain came, and the next morning her husband's boat was back at the shore. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, Lamb of God, you are our Passover. Our Lady of Mount Carmel, mother of the Lamb, pray with us. Amen.
share: When I see the blood, I will pass over you (Exodus 12:13). Where have I experienced God passing over me, sparing me from something worse?
I will lift up the cup of salvation (Psalm 116:13). How can I bring my thanksgiving at the Mass to a new depth this week?
Look, a little cloud no bigger than a person's hand (1 Kings 18:44). What small sign of hope is God showing me in a time of waiting?
pm.resp: I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the Passover of Christ with gratitude and mercy.
For the Carmelite family, in Kerala and throughout the world, and for all who wear the scapular.
For farmers and fishermen, and for a monsoon that brings life and not harm.
For all who are waiting and praying for something for a long time, that they may not give up.
For our group, that following Mary we may do whatever Jesus tells us.
pm.close: Father, you gave us Christ, the Lamb, and Mary, his mother and ours. Through her intercession and example, lead us to your Son who lives and reigns with you for ever and ever. Amen.

quick: The Israelites leave Egypt after four hundred and thirty years, with a mixed crowd of other people, and the Lord keeps vigil that night.
Some Pharisees plot to destroy Jesus; he withdraws, heals the crowds and asks them to keep silent.
Matthew quotes Isaiah: the Servant is gentle, he will not break a bruised reed, and the Gentiles will hope in his name.
2027-07-17.action: Say a kind and encouraging word today to someone who is discouraged.
2027-07-17.question: When I meet someone who is fragile, do I snap the reed, or do I bend down to help?

family.explain: Jesus was kind to everybody, especially the people who were sad, sick or weak. The prophet Isaiah had said that God's Servant would be like that: he would never break a bent reed, or put out a flame that was nearly gone. Think of a candle that is nearly out. A gentle hand shields it, and it burns again. Jesus is like that with us. When we are sad or have done wrong, he does not shout; he helps us to burn brightly again.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad, lonely or discouraged, and we ask Jesus to make us gentle with others.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or school is feeling bent or tired this week? What small thing can we do to help them shine again?”

illus: An illustration

In a village in Wayanad, a retired schoolteacher kept an old kerosene lamp in her house although there was electricity. When the power failed in the monsoon nights she would light it, and the children of the neighbourhood would gather. The wick was always almost gone, she said, and a breath too strong would put it out, so she lit it with a cupped hand. She told the children that one learns more from the weak flame than from the strong light, because it teaches you to shield what is small. Years later, one of those children became a nurse and said that she remembered the lamp whenever she met a patient who had no strength left. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you who keep watch over us, strengthen us in your gentleness. Lord Jesus, chosen Servant, teach us your way. Amen.
share: That was for the Lord a night of vigil (Exodus 12:42). When have I felt that God was keeping watch over me in a dark time?
A mixed crowd also went up with them (Exodus 12:38). Who is on the edge of my community, and how can I welcome them?
He will not break a bruised reed (Matthew 12:20). Whom do I know who is a bruised reed, and what does Jesus' way suggest that I do?
pm.resp: His steadfast love endures for ever.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a gentle mother to the weak, the doubting and the wounded.
For those who work at night, and those who keep watch beside the sick and dying.
For refugees, migrants and strangers who journey among us, that they may find welcome.
For people who are discouraged, depressed or on the brink of giving up.
For our group, that we may be gentle, patient and hopeful, like Christ the Servant.
pm.close: Father, you watched over your people in the night and sent your Servant to heal. Make us gentle with the fragile and faithful in our watching. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Pharaoh pursues Israel to the sea; the people panic, and Moses says: Do not be afraid, stand firm; the Lord will fight for you.
The Lord tells Moses: Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
Jesus refuses a proof to those who demand one, and promises only the sign of Jonah: his three days in the heart of the earth.
2027-07-19.action: Take one small step today toward the thing you are afraid to face, after praying Moses' words.
2027-07-19.question: When I am afraid, do I only cry out, or do I also trust and go forward when the Lord says go?

family.explain: The people of Israel had left Egypt, but then they looked back and saw the king's army coming after them, and in front of them was the sea! They were very frightened. Moses said: do not be afraid. The Lord will fight for you. God made a path through the sea, and all the people walked across on dry ground. Whenever we feel there is no way out, we can remember that God made a way in the sea.
family.intention: We pray for families who are afraid or in trouble, and for people whose homes are in danger from the monsoon floods.
family.ask: Ask: “When were we afraid as a family, and how did God help us? Can we thank him tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a low-lying village near the Periyar one monsoon night, the river rose faster than anyone expected and the only road went under water. The village was frightened. An old woman who had lived through many floods went from house to house with a lamp and said the same thing at every door: do not be afraid; stay together; keep the children upstairs; I have already told the boatmen at the next bend. At first light two country boats came, and every family got across. Afterwards a neighbour asked her how she had stayed so calm. She said: my mother used to tell me what Moses said: stand firm and see what the Lord will do today. But she also said that Moses was told: go forward. So I prayed, and then I sent the boy to the boatmen. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you open a way where we see none. Lord Jesus, sign of Jonah, risen from the dead, make us stand firm and go forward in faith. Amen.
share: Do not be afraid, stand firm (Exodus 14:13). Which fear in my life most needs to hear these words?
Tell the Israelites to go forward (Exodus 14:15). Is there a step God is asking me to take while I stand wondering?
Something greater than Jonah is here (Matthew 12:41). In what way do I still ask Jesus for proof rather than trust his word?
pm.resp: I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously.
interc: For the Church, that she may trust the Lord who fights for her and go forward in mission.
For all who are afraid today: the sick, the unemployed, the people living in flood-prone places, and refugees.
For those who pass through the waters of baptism, and for their godparents and families.
For the Jewish people, who first sang the Song of Moses, and for peace among all the children of Abraham.
For our group, that we may seek not signs but the Lord himself.
pm.close: Father, you saved your people through the sea and your Son from the grave. Make us stand firm in trial and sing your praise. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: On the night of the sea the Lord drives the water back, Israel walks through on dry ground, and the Egyptian army is swallowed up.
Seeing the great work of the Lord, the people fear him, believe in him and in Moses, and sing.
Jesus says that those who do the will of his Father are his brother and sister and mother.
2027-07-20.action: Make the sign of the cross with holy water today with the thought: I belong to God's family.
2027-07-20.question: Whose needs in my own family and parish am I called to serve, because we are brothers and sisters in the Lord?
kidsaint: St Apollinaris

Apollinaris was a bishop in the city of Ravenna in Italy, a very long time ago. Old stories say that he was a friend of St Peter, who sent him to tell the people of Ravenna about Jesus. He cared for the people like a shepherd who cares for sheep, and he suffered a great deal for his faith. In the church of Sant'Apollinare in Classe there is a beautiful old picture of him in the middle of a green field with sheep around him. Lesson: a shepherd's love is stronger than fear.

family.explain: Jesus was talking to many people. His mother and his relatives came and stood outside, wanting to speak to him. Jesus pointed to his friends and said: whoever does what my Father in heaven wants is my brother and sister and mother. Mary always did what God asked, so she is the best example for all of us. Each one of us can be in Jesus' family by listening to God and doing his word.
family.intention: We pray for our parents, brothers and sisters and for all our relatives, and for people who have no family.
family.ask: Ask: “What does God want us to do this week as a family? Let us choose one thing and do it.”

illus: An illustration

A young man who had left his village in the south of Kerala to work in a city far away once told his parish priest that the loneliest night of his life was his first. He had a room, a job and a phone, but no one who knew his name. On Sunday he went into the nearest church, and an old woman sitting beside him shared her prayer book without a word. After Mass a family asked him to come home for tea. Years later he said: I had been told that the Church is a family, but that Sunday was the first time I felt it. I was no longer a stranger. Jesus had said that those who do the Father's will are his brothers and sisters, and some strangers were doing it. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Father, you gather your people through water and word. Lord Jesus, make us your family, doing the Father's will after the example of Mary. Amen.
share: The Israelites went into the sea on dry ground (Exodus 14:22). What does it mean to me that I was brought through the waters of baptism?
The people feared the Lord and believed in the Lord (Exodus 14:31). Which moment in my life made my faith real?
Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother (Matthew 12:50). What does the Father ask of me today?
pm.resp: Sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously.
interc: For the Church, the family of God, that she may be a home for the lonely and the stranger.
For bishops and priests, especially those who are shepherds like St Apollinaris, that they may love their flocks.
For the newly baptised and their families.
For families divided by quarrels or distance, that they may be reconciled.
For Mary's children everywhere, that like her they may hear the word of God and keep it.
pm.close: Father, you make us your children in baptism. Help us do your will and welcome one another as brothers and sisters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The hungry Israelites grumble in the wilderness; the Lord promises bread from heaven, enough for each day, and sends quails and manna.
Moses says of the manna: It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat; the psalm remembers it as the bread of angels.
Jesus sits in a boat and tells the parable of the sower: seed on the path, on rocks, among thorns, and on good soil that bears a hundredfold.
2027-07-21.action: Say grace slowly before each meal today, and give something to feed the hungry.
2027-07-21.question: What kind of soil is my heart today: the path, the rock, the thorns, or good soil?
kidsaint: St Lawrence of Brindisi

Lawrence was born in Italy and became a Capuchin friar when he was only sixteen years old. He loved the Bible very much, and he could speak many languages: Latin, Hebrew, Greek, German, French and more. He travelled to many countries to tell people about Jesus. Once, when a big army was going to fight, he rode in front of the soldiers holding a crucifix high and said: forward, God is with us! Lesson: God's word makes us brave, and learning to listen to it is the first step to sharing it.

family.explain: Jesus sat in a boat by the lake and told a story. A farmer went out to sow seed. Some seed fell on the path, and the birds ate it. Some fell on rocks, and the little plants dried up. Some fell among thorns, and the thorns choked it. But some seed fell on good soil, and it grew into lots of grain. God's word is the seed. We want our hearts to be good soil. And long ago in the desert, God sent bread from heaven every morning to feed his hungry people, and he still takes care of us every day.
family.intention: We pray for children and families who are hungry and for farmers whose crops depend on the rains.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to make our hearts good soil: pray together, read the Bible, forgive one another?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish in the hills of Wayanad once taught a boy who seemed to hear nothing. He sat at the back, looked out of the window and left as soon as the bell rang. The teacher prayed for him each year and never knew what became of him. Twelve years later a letter arrived from a Gulf country, written by the boy, now a man working on road building. He wrote: I never told you, but I remember everything you said about the sower. Last year my friend died in an accident, and that night I could not sleep; the only prayer that came to me was one you taught us. Then I went to a priest. The seed took twelve years, but it grew. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you feed us day by day. Lord Jesus, Sower of the word, make our hearts good soil. Amen.
share: The whole congregation complained (Exodus 16:2). What do I grumble about, and what would change if I thanked God for the bread I already have?
It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat (Exodus 16:15). Which of God's gifts do I take for granted?
Other seeds fell on good soil (Matthew 13:8). What is the biggest obstacle to the word growing in me, the path, the rock or the thorns?
pm.resp: The Lord gave them bread from heaven.
interc: For the Church, that she may feed the world with the word and the Bread of Life.
For people who are hungry today, and for all who work to feed them.
For priests, catechists and preachers, that like St Lawrence of Brindisi they may sow the word with love.
For farmers and for rain in its season, that the harvest may be abundant.
For our group, that we may be good soil for the word of God.
pm.close: Father, you give us daily bread and the word of life. Make us good soil, and let your word bear fruit in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mary Magdalene comes to the tomb in the dark, finds the stone rolled away, and runs to Peter and the beloved disciple.
She stays, weeping, outside the tomb; the angels ask why she weeps, and the risen Jesus, whom she takes for the gardener, calls her by name: Mary!
Jesus tells her not to cling to him and sends her to his brothers; she announces: I have seen the Lord.
2027-07-22.action: Tell one person this week, in your own words, what the risen Lord has done for you.
2027-07-22.question: Do I stay with the Lord when others have gone home, and do I recognise his voice when he calls me by name?
catechism: Who were the first witnesses of the Resurrection?
Why did the apostles at first not believe?
Why is Sunday called the Lord's day?
kidsaint: St Mary Magdalene

Mary Magdalene was a friend and follower of Jesus. She loved him very much. Jesus had healed her when she was very sick, and from that day she followed him with other women and helped to take care of him and his friends. When Jesus died on the cross, she stayed close. On Sunday morning, very early, she went to his tomb and cried because he was not there. Then someone called her name: Mary! It was Jesus, alive! He sent her to tell his friends. So she was the first person to tell the good news of Easter. Lesson: when you love Jesus, he calls you by name and sends you to tell others about him.
2027-07-22.special: Feast of St Mary Magdalene. Gloria; no Creed. White. The apostle of the apostles, the first witness of the Resurrection.
term: A title for Mary Magdalene (in Latin apostola apostolorum), used since the early centuries and by St Thomas Aquinas. “Apostle” means “one who is sent.” Mary was sent by the risen Lord to the apostles with the news of the Resurrection. The title does not make her one of the Twelve; it honours her as the first messenger of Easter. In 2016 her memorial was raised to the rank of a feast.

family.explain: Mary Magdalene was crying outside the empty tomb, because she missed Jesus so much. She did not know that Jesus was standing right behind her! Then he said her name: Mary! She turned and said: Teacher! Then Jesus said: go and tell my friends. So Mary ran to the disciples and said: I have seen the Lord! She was the first person ever to tell that Jesus is alive.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad or have lost someone they love, and for people who tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we tell this week that Jesus is alive? Let us each choose one person and say to them: Jesus loves you.”

illus: An illustration

In a coastal parish near Alappuzha the first person at the church door every morning was an old widow called Mariamma, who came before dawn to light the lamps for the 5.30 Mass. Often she was there before the priest. A child once asked her why she came so early. She said: the first people at the tomb were women, and they came before the sun was up. Somebody has to be there first, so that the others can be told. When she grew too old to climb the church steps, a girl from the catechism class took over the keys and lit the lamps before dawn. The priest later said that he had never preached a better sermon on Mary Magdalene than that widow's answer. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called Mary of Magdala by her name. Call us, and send us to proclaim that you are risen. Amen.
share: I sought him whom my soul loves (Song of Songs 3:1). What am I seeking in the dark hours of my life?
Woman, why are you weeping? (John 20:15). What is the sorrow I bring to the Lord today?
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” (John 20:16). How do I hear the Lord calling my name?
I have seen the Lord (John 20:18). What would I say if I were asked to give witness to my faith?
pm.resp: My soul is thirsting for you, O Lord my God.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary Magdalene she may be a faithful witness of the Resurrection to the end.
For women in the Church and in the world, that their witness and gifts may be honoured.
For those who weep, the bereaved and the lonely, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
For those who seek the Lord in the dark, in doubt or in sorrow, that they may find him.
For our group, that we may proclaim the Easter good news to those around us.
pm.close: Father, you made Mary Magdalene the first witness and herald of the Resurrection. Grant that we, too, may see the Lord and announce him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Sinai God speaks the Ten Words, beginning with I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
The psalm sings that the law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul, and sweeter than honey.
Jesus explains the parable of the sower: the path, the rocky ground, the thorns and the good soil that hears the word, understands it and bears fruit.
2027-07-23.action: Read the Ten Commandments slowly today and pray for help with the one that is hardest for you.
2027-07-23.question: Which kind of soil is my heart when I hear the word of God: the path, the rock, the thorns or good soil?
kidsaint: St Bridget of Sweden

Bridget lived in Sweden, a country in the cold north, a long time ago. She was a rich lady who married a good man and had eight children. She loved to pray and to think about how much Jesus suffered for us. When her husband died, she gave much of her money to the poor and started an order of sisters and brothers. She travelled to Rome, and then to the Holy Land, where Jesus lived. Lesson: you can be a mother or father and also a saint; what matters is that God's word takes root in your heart.

family.explain: God gave his people ten important rules, the Ten Commandments. They help us to love God and love other people. God said: I am the Lord your God, and I brought you out of slavery. Then he said: do not steal, do not lie, honor your father and mother, and love only God above everything. Jesus said that all the rules are about love. And Jesus told a story about seeds and different kinds of soil: the soil is our heart, and God's word is the seed.
family.intention: We pray for our parents and grandparents, and for people who find it difficult to forgive or to be honest.
family.ask: Ask: “Which rule is the hardest for me? How can we help each other to keep it this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grocer in a small town in central Kerala hung a small board over his weighing scale: Honest weight, because someone is watching. Customers smiled, thinking it was a joke. One day during the monsoon, when the river road was cut and the shop next door ran out of rice, a woman who had bought from him for years was told by the other grocer that there was nothing left. She walked through the rain to the honest scale. Years later she told her grandchildren: I did not know about God's law then, I only knew that I could trust the man with the scale. His board was a sermon on the seventh and eighth commandments. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you give us your law as a gift. Lord Jesus, write it on our hearts and make us good soil. Amen.
share: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt (Exodus 20:2). How is God's law a gift of freedom in my own life?
The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul (Psalm 19:7). When has a commandment of the Lord given me life?
This is the one who hears the word and understands it (Matthew 13:23). What stops the word from taking root in me?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of everlasting life.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the commandments of God as a path to freedom and joy.
For parents and grandparents, who teach the commandments to the young by their lives.
For those who are in prison, bound by sin or addiction, that the Lord who brought Israel out of slavery may release them.
For men and women who read and preach the word of God, that they may be good soil.
For widows, mothers and women of prayer, after the example of St Bridget.
pm.close: Father, you give your law out of love and write it on our hearts through your Son. Keep us faithful to your word and bring us to its fruit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses writes down the words of the Lord, builds an altar with twelve pillars, and reads the book of the covenant; the people say: we will do, and we will be obedient.
Moses sprinkles the blood of the sacrifice on the altar and on the people: the blood of the covenant.
Jesus tells the parable of the wheat and the weeds: let both grow together until the harvest.
2027-07-24.action: Choose one thing you heard at Mass this weekend, and do it.
2027-07-24.question: Do I judge quickly who is wheat and who is a weed, or do I leave judgement to God and pray for everyone?
kidsaint: St Sharbel Makhluf

Sharbel was a shepherd boy in the mountains of Lebanon, a country in the Middle East. He loved to pray alone in a cave while his sheep grazed. When he grew up he became a monk, and later a hermit, which means a person who lives alone to pray. He lived in a tiny room on a mountain, ate very simple food and prayed for hours for everyone in the world. When he died, many people came to his tomb to pray, and many were healed. Lesson: a prayer said quietly and secretly is not lost; God sees it and uses it for the good of many.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a farmer who planted good wheat in his field. In the night, an enemy came and planted weeds in the same field. When the plants grew, the farmer's workers saw the weeds, too. They asked: should we pull them out? The farmer said: no, you will pull up the wheat too. Wait until the harvest. In God's field, good people and bad people are growing side by side, and God is patient with all. He gives everyone time to change.
family.intention: We pray for people who find it hard to be good, and for the patience to wait for them.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we are quick to judge? What can we do this week to give them a chance?”

illus: An illustration

A rice farmer from Kuttanad, an old man named Ouseph, used to tell his grandchildren that the worst weed in the paddy field is the grass that looks exactly like the young rice. A new worker, hired in a hurry, once pulled up half the good seedlings in one morning, because they all looked alike to her. Ouseph never scolded her. He said: in the first weeks only the Lord can tell them apart. We must wait until the ear shows. Years later the same woman supervised the field herself, and was known for the patience with which she weeded. When someone in the parish spoke harshly about a neighbour, she would say: wait until the harvest. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: God of the covenant, you pour out your life for us. Lord Jesus, give us the patience of the householder and the thankfulness of those who offer a sacrifice of praise. Amen.
share: All the words that the Lord has spoken we will do (Exodus 24:3). What have I said to God that I have not yet done?
See the blood of the covenant (Exodus 24:8). What does it mean for me that Christ's blood binds me to God and to my brothers and sisters?
Let both of them grow together until the harvest (Matthew 13:30). Whom do I judge too fast, and how can I give them time?
pm.resp: To the upright I will show the saving power of God.
interc: For the Church, a field where wheat and weeds grow together, that she may be patient and holy.
For the Maronite Church and the Christians of Lebanon, and for peace in Lebanon and in the Middle East, through the intercession of St Sharbel.
For those who live in silence and hidden prayer, hermits, monks and nuns, that their prayer may bear fruit.
For those who are sick, that through the intercession of St Sharbel they may find healing and hope.
For our group, that we may be doers of the word and not hearers only.
pm.close: Father, you made a covenant with your people by sacrifice and sealed it in the blood of your Son. Make us faithful to your word and patient with one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses finds the people dancing around a golden calf, breaks the tablets, and then goes back up the mountain to plead for them.
Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed and to yeast: small beginnings that grow from within.
Sts Joachim and Anne, the parents of Mary, are remembered as the hidden people who handed on the faith.
2027-07-26.action: Ask a grandparent or an elderly relative to tell you one story of faith from your family.
2027-07-26.question: Whom am I praying for by name, as Moses prayed, and whom did God use to plant the faith in me?
kidsaint: Sts Joachim and Anne

An old book tells us that Joachim and Anne were Mary's parents. They were not young, and they had no children, and they prayed and prayed. Then God gave them a little daughter, Mary, and they taught her to pray the psalms. So Joachim and Anne were the grandparents of Jesus! We do not know many details, and some of the stories are only stories. But we know that grandparents are very special. Many children in Kerala are named Anna or Annamma after St Anne. Lesson: grandparents who pray plant seeds of faith that grow into trees.

family.explain: A mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice. But planted in the ground it grows into a big plant where birds make their nests. Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like that: it begins small and grows. Joachim and Anne were Mary's parents; they loved her and taught her to pray. Their small love grew into something huge, because Mary became the mother of Jesus. Our small prayers and kind acts can grow too.
family.intention: We thank God for our grandparents and for those who taught us to pray, and we pray for those who are far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “What did your grandparents teach you? Who taught them to pray? Shall we ask them to tell us?”

illus: An illustration

In a Kerala house the evening prayer was always led by the grandmother. She sat on the veranda mat with a rosary, and the grandchildren, tired and sleepy, sat around her and answered the Hail Marys. The grandson grew up, left the village and became a priest. At her funeral he said: I never once heard her give a sermon, but I learned from her what prayer is. My first prayer was in her lap. The seed was so small that none of us noticed it being sown. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord God, you hid the beginnings of our salvation in a quiet family. Teach us to hand on the faith and to pray for those who have strayed. Amen.
share: I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin (Exodus 32:30). For whom would I be ready to stand in the breach?
The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed (Matthew 13:31). What small beginning in my family or parish do I think too little to matter?
Who were the Joachim and Anne in my own life, the ones who first taught me to pray, and how can I thank God for them today?
pm.resp: Remember us, O Lord, as you favor your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may always intercede for the world as Moses did, and hand on the faith to the next generation.
For grandparents and parents, that they may be signs of God's patience and teachers of prayer.
For children and young people who have never heard a prayer at home, and for those who have turned away from the faith.
For couples who long for a child, that, like Joachim and Anne, they may wait and pray in hope.
For our group, that we may be small seeds and hidden yeast for the kingdom.
pm.close: God of our fathers, you gave the Blessed Virgin Mary a father and a mother who taught her your promises. Give us a faith that we can hand on. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses pitches a tent of meeting outside the camp, where the Lord speaks to him face to face, as to a friend; Joshua will not leave the tent.
The Lord proclaims his name to Moses: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Jesus explains the parable of the weeds: the Son of Man sows, the harvest is the end of the age, and the righteous will shine like the sun.
2027-07-27.action: Spend ten quiet minutes today talking to God as to a friend.
2027-07-27.question: Am I patient with the weeds I see in others and in myself, or do I want to pull everything up now?
kidsaint: Moses, the friend of God

Moses had a special tent where he went to talk to God. The people stood at the doors of their own tents and watched, and when the big cloud came down they all bowed. The Bible says that God spoke to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. Moses was not perfect, but he kept coming back to talk to God and he asked God to forgive his people. Lesson: God wants to be our friend, and we can talk to him anywhere, any time.

family.explain: Moses had a tent where he went to talk to God, and God spoke to him like a friend. We can talk to God like that too, in church or in our room. In the Gospel Jesus tells a story about a farmer who sowed good seed, but an enemy sowed weeds in the field. The farmer said: do not pull up the weeds now, or you will pull up the wheat. Let both grow until the harvest. God is patient with us, even when we do wrong, and he gives us time to grow.
family.intention: We pray for those who find it hard to forgive and for people we find difficult.
family.ask: Ask: “Where can we each find a quiet place to talk to God? Who needs our patience this week?”

illus: An illustration

A farmer in Kuttanad who tended his paddy through the monsoon told a young neighbour that the hardest part was not planting but weeding. When the young man pulled up weeds in a hurry, he often pulled out the rice with them. The old farmer said: you wait until the weed shows itself, and you pull only what you are sure of. Years later the young man, now a school headmaster, used the same lesson with a boy who was always in trouble. He waited, and he watched, and one day the boy brought him a prize from a science fair. The headmaster said it was the wheat that had been growing all along. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Merciful and gracious God, you speak to us as friends and you are slow to anger. Teach us to listen, to be patient and to trust your harvest. Amen.
share: The Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend (Exodus 33:11). When did I last speak to God as to a friend?
The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious (Exodus 34:6). Which word in this name of God do I most need to hear today?
Let both of them grow together until the harvest (Matthew 13:30). Whom do I need to be more patient with?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For the Church, a field of wheat and weeds, that she may be a place of patience, mercy and conversion.
For priests and confessors, that they may show the mercy of the God who is slow to anger.
For farmers and labourers who tend the young crops in the rain, and for a good harvest.
For those who judge others harshly, and for those who have been judged unfairly, that all may find God's mercy.
For our group, that we may pray as friends of God and be patient with each other.
pm.close: Father, you are merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love. Keep us patient until the harvest and bring us to shine in your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses comes down Sinai with a shining face, and does not know it; he veils it and unveils it before the Lord.
Jesus compares the kingdom to a treasure hidden in a field and a pearl of great value: the finder joyfully sells all.
St Alphonsa, a hidden Clarist sister of Kerala who offered her sufferings in love, is the first woman of Indian origin canonised.
catechism: How can suffering unite us with Christ?
Why does the Church canonise saints?
kidsaint: St Alphonsa

Alphonsa's first name was Annakutty, and she lived in Kerala. Her mother died when she was little, and she grew up loving Jesus very much. When she was older she became a sister in a convent at Bharananganam and was given the name Alphonsa. She was often sick, and sometimes she was in pain, but she never complained. She offered her pain to Jesus for other people, and she was kind to everyone. When she died in 1946 she was only thirty-five. Many people pray at her tomb, and in 2008 the Pope declared her a saint. She is the first woman from India to be made a saint. Lesson: even small, quiet things done with love for Jesus shine like light.
2027-07-28.special: Memorial of St Alphonsa (India): weekday readings of Week 17; first woman of Indian origin to be canonised (12 October 2008).
term: The solemn act by which the Pope declares that a deceased member of the faithful lived heroic holiness, is in heaven with God, and may be honoured by the whole Church as a saint and invoked as an intercessor. The process normally goes through the titles Servant of God, Venerable, Blessed (beatification, usually after one miracle through the person's intercession) and Saint (canonisation, usually after a second miracle) (Catechism 828).

family.explain: Jesus tells a short story: a man found a treasure in a field. He was so happy that he sold everything he had and bought the field. Jesus is the greatest treasure of all. St Alphonsa loved Jesus so much that she gave her whole life to him. Even when she was ill and in pain, she smiled and was kind, and she prayed for other people. Today she is a saint, and we can ask her to pray for us.
family.intention: We pray for the sick and for people who are in pain, and we thank God for St Alphonsa.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the best thing that we have found in our family? How can we show Jesus' light to others this week?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher from a village near Pala went to Bharananganam every year on the day before the new school year began. She would light a candle at the tomb of St Alphonsa, and standing there she would say a short prayer for each child in her class by name, naming the quiet ones twice. She said she was not asking for results in examinations; she asked for the grace to be patient. When she retired, a former pupil told her: I always knew that someone was praying for me. She had never once told them about the candle. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the treasure and the pearl. Make us joyful finders, ready to give all, and let our hidden lives shine with your light. Amen.
share: Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone (Exodus 34:29). What might others see in me that I do not see?
He goes and sells all that he has and buys that field (Matthew 13:44). What is the treasure that I have found, and what is it asking of me?
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies (John 12:24). What hidden suffering of mine could be offered for others?
pm.resp: Holy is the Lord our God.
interc: For the Church in India, in all her rites, that she may honour her saints and live the Gospel with joy.
For the Franciscan Clarist sisters and all religious women, that their hidden lives may bear fruit for the Church.
For the sick, especially those in long illness, that they may find in St Alphonsa a friend and be united with Christ's passion.
For young people discerning a vocation, that they may find the pearl and be generous.
For our group, that we may carry the light of Christ gently into our homes and work.
pm.close: God of holiness, you make your glory shine in the lives of your saints. By the prayers of St Alphonsa, make us treasure Christ above all things. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses sets up the tabernacle as the Lord commanded, and the cloud covers the tent while the glory of the Lord fills it.
Martha goes out to meet Jesus and confesses: you are the Messiah, the Son of God; Jesus says: I am the resurrection and the life.
Martha, Mary and Lazarus of Bethany are remembered together as friends who gave Jesus a home.
2027-07-29.action: Make a place in your home or in your day to sit quietly with the Lord for ten minutes.
2027-07-29.question: When I am busy with many things, do I make room for the one thing that is necessary?
kidsaint: Martha, Mary and Lazarus

Martha, Mary and their brother Lazarus lived in a village called Bethany, and Jesus was their friend. He loved to visit. Martha cooked and cleaned and wanted everything to be just right. Mary sat down by Jesus' feet and listened to him. Jesus said to Martha: dear Martha, you are worried about so many things, but Mary has chosen the best part. When Lazarus died, Jesus cried, and then he called Lazarus back to life! Lesson: it is good to help, but we must also take time to sit with Jesus and listen.

family.explain: Jesus visited the house of his friends Martha and Mary. Martha was busy cooking and cleaning, and Mary sat at Jesus' feet to listen. Martha got upset and asked Jesus to tell Mary to help. Jesus said: Martha, you are worried about many things, but only one thing is really important. Mary has chosen the better part. It is good to serve, and it is also good to sit still and listen to Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for those who cook and care for us at home, and we pray for families who have lost someone they love.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we sit quietly with Jesus? How could we make our evening prayer a time of listening, and not only of saying words?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in the hills of Idukki the women who cooked for the feast every year were led by an old woman, Marthamma, who was always on her feet and never sat in church. The young priest once teased her that she had no time for Jesus. She laughed and said: my prayer is the rice. He did not answer. The next year, after the feast, he sat her down in the front pew with a cup of tea and said: now you listen for ten minutes. She wept quietly. The priest said afterwards that he could not tell which of them had learned more. Jesus loves both the cooking and the listening, and does not want us to lose either. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord Jesus, friend of Martha, Mary and Lazarus, come into our homes. Teach us to serve and to listen, and to believe that you are the resurrection and the life. Amen.
share: Moses did everything just as the Lord had commanded him (Exodus 40:16). Where is the Lord asking me to do as he commands, even in small things?
Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). What have I said to the Lord at a time of loss, and how did he answer?
Mary has chosen the better part (Luke 10:42). What would it mean to make Mary's choice today?
pm.resp: How lovely is your dwelling place, Lord, mighty God.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where Christ is welcome and the Word is heard.
For those who cook, clean and care for others at home, often unseen, that their service be honoured.
For those who mourn a brother, sister or friend, that they may hear Jesus say: I am the resurrection and the life.
For the sick and the dying, and for those who accompany them.
For our group, that we may welcome Christ into our homes and listen to him.
pm.close: Father, your Son found a home among friends in Bethany. Give us the faith to welcome him, the love to serve him and the hope of rising with him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord appoints the festivals of Israel: Passover, first fruits, the fifty days, the Day of Atonement and Booths.
In Nazareth the people are astounded by Jesus' wisdom but take offense at him, because they think they know him.
Jesus does not do many deeds of power in Nazareth because of the people's unbelief.
2027-07-30.action: Go to Mass or pray today as if you were meeting Jesus for the first time.
2027-07-30.question: What familiar part of my faith am I no longer seeing, and how can I look at it again?
kidsaint: St Peter Chrysologus

Peter was a bishop in a city called Ravenna in Italy, a long time ago. He was a wonderful preacher, but he did not give long sermons. His sermons were short, clear and full of lovely pictures, so people loved to listen. They called him Chrysologus, which means golden word. He taught that prayer, fasting and kindness to the poor belong together. Lesson: a few good words, said with love, are worth more than many long ones.

family.explain: Jesus went back to Nazareth, where he had grown up, and taught in the synagogue. People were amazed, but then they said: he is only the carpenter's son! We know his mother and his family. They did not believe in him, and Jesus did not do many miracles there. Sometimes we think we know someone very well and we forget how special they are. Let us look at each other, at our parish and at the Mass with new eyes!
family.intention: We thank God for the feasts and Sundays that fill the year with joy, and we pray for people who have stopped believing.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we do on Sundays and feast days that makes them special? What could we do to make them more joyful?”

illus: An illustration

An old sacristan in a church in Kottayam district had opened the same door at five o'clock every morning for forty years. A young visitor asked him whether he was tired of it. He said: some mornings I almost forget why I am doing it. And then I think that he is there, in the tabernacle, waiting for me as he was waiting for my father and my grandfather, and I feel as if I am opening the door for the first time. He said it was the one thing he prayed for: never to take the open door for granted. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord of holy time, you come near on appointed days and on ordinary days. Open our eyes to know you. Amen.
share: These are the appointed festivals of the Lord (Leviticus 23:4). Which of the Church's feasts and seasons helps me most to meet him?
Where did this man get this wisdom? (Matthew 13:54). What in my faith have I stopped seeing because it is so familiar?
He did not do many deeds of power there, because of their unbelief (Matthew 13:58). Where might my own unbelief hold back what the Lord wants to do?
pm.resp: Sing with joy to God our help.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the feasts with joy and welcome Christ afresh each day.
For the Jewish people, who keep the appointed festivals of the Lord, that they may be blessed in the covenant God has made with them.
For preachers and teachers, that like St Peter Chrysologus they may speak the Word with clarity and warmth.
For those who have grown tired of their faith, or taken the Lord for granted.
For our group, that we may meet the Lord with fresh eyes.
pm.close: Father, you give your people times and seasons to meet you. Make us ready to welcome your Son, who comes in the ordinary and the holy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The law of the Jubilee: every fiftieth year the trumpet proclaims liberty and every family returns to its land.
Herod Antipas, afraid of the crowd and of his guests, has John the Baptist beheaded in prison.
St Ignatius of Loyola, converted by a wound, founds the Society of Jesus for the greater glory of God.
2027-07-31.action: Forgive a debt or a wrong today, as the Jubilee asks, and do one task for the glory of God.
2027-07-31.question: Whose freedom or good name am I keeping back, and what am I afraid to lose?
kidsaint: St Ignatius of Loyola

Ignatius was a soldier in Spain who dreamed of fame. One day a cannonball hurt his leg very badly, and he had to stay in bed for months. There was nothing to read except books about Jesus and the saints. He began to think: the saints did great things for God. I can too! So he gave his life to God, and he gathered friends who wanted to help others for God's glory. They were called Jesuits. One of them, Francis Xavier, went all the way to India. Ignatius had a saying: for the greater glory of God. Lesson: even a hurt, when given to God, can turn into a new beginning.

family.explain: King Herod had put John the Baptist in prison because John told him the truth. Herod was afraid of what people thought. At a big party he made a rash promise, and because he did not want to look foolish in front of his guests, he did something very wrong. John was a brave man who told the truth even though it cost him his life. His friends took care of his body and went and told Jesus. We can always bring our sadness to Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who suffer for telling the truth, and for those who are afraid to do what is right.
family.ask: Ask: “Have we ever been afraid to do the right thing because of what others would say? How can we be braver?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolboy in a Jesuit school in Tamil Nadu used to write A.M.D.G. at the top of every exercise book. His teacher, an old Jesuit brother, told him that it stood for the greater glory of God. Years later the boy, now a doctor in a village clinic in Kerala, wrote the same letters on the first page of every patient's file. When a young nurse asked what they meant, he said: they remind me that the patient is not here for my glory, or for the clinic's, but because God wishes to be glorified in someone's recovery. The nurse began writing the letters too. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord of the Jubilee, release us from fear and from the need to please others, and teach us to do everything for your greater glory. Amen.
share: You shall proclaim liberty throughout the land (Leviticus 25:10). Whom do I need to release, or from what do I need to be released?
Herod feared the crowd and his guests (Matthew 14:5, 9). Where does the fear of what others think hold me back from doing right?
Do everything for the glory of God (1 Corinthians 10:31). What ordinary task will I do for God's glory today?
pm.resp: O God, let all the nations praise you!
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim liberty to captives and good news to the poor.
For the Society of Jesus and all religious, that they may serve for the greater glory of God.
For those who are imprisoned unjustly, and for those who suffer for speaking the truth.
For those who are bound by debt, fear or addiction, that they may know the freedom of the children of God.
For our group, that we may do everything for the glory of God.
pm.close: God and Father of all nations, you sent your Son to proclaim liberty. By the prayers of St Ignatius, give us liberty to offer ourselves wholly to you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the feast of St Thomas, and for us in India it is a very special feast. According to the tradition that our fathers have kept for nearly two thousand years, this apostle crossed the sea, came to our coast, preached, baptised, and gave his life for Christ. We are the heirs of that story. Many of our families can trace their faith back to him. Today let us give thanks.

But we know Thomas best from the Gospel we have just heard, and I want to say first that the Church does not remember him as a failure. In John's Gospel he appears three times. The first time he says: Let us also go, that we may die with him (John 11:16). Thomas is the one who is ready to follow Jesus to death, when others hesitate. The second time he says: Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way? (John 14:5). He asks the honest question, and because of it we have the answer: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. And the third time is the scene we heard today.

On Easter evening Thomas was not with the others. Perhaps he could not bear to be in that room; perhaps he was grieving by himself. When they tell him, we have seen the Lord, he says: Unless I see the mark of the nails... I will not believe (John 20:25). We are very hard on Thomas. But he asks for nothing that the others had not already been given. They too had been shown his hands and his side. Thomas is asking to be on the same footing as his friends.

And what does Jesus do? He does not scold. A week later, on the same day of the week, the first day, the day we gather for Mass, he comes through closed doors and says: Peace be with you. Then he turns to Thomas, the doubter, and gives him exactly what he asked for: Put your finger here and see my hands (John 20:27). Dear friends, how gentle is our Lord with honest doubt! If you have questions about your faith, do not hide them. Bring them to him. Bring them to a priest or a catechist. The Lord is not afraid of them.

And Thomas answers with the highest confession of faith in the whole Gospel: My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). Then Jesus looks past Thomas and speaks to us: Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe (John 20:29). That means every one of us in this church. We have not seen his wounds, but we have seen his love in the saints, in our parents, in the sacraments. Every time we kneel at the consecration, we say the words of Thomas: My Lord and my God. Let us say them today with all our hearts, and let us ask St Thomas to keep India faithful to the Lord whom he loved and for whom he died.
kids: Children, today is the feast of St Thomas, one of the twelve friends of Jesus. After Jesus rose from the dead, Thomas was not there when Jesus came to see his friends. They told him, but he said: I need to see it myself! A week later Jesus came again and said to Thomas: look at my hands. And Thomas said: My Lord and my God! He believed. Jesus said: happy are those who believe even when they cannot see. That is us! A long time ago, according to tradition, Thomas travelled all the way to India, and the Christians of Kerala say he told our country about Jesus. Let us say thank you to St Thomas, and let us say his prayer: My Lord and my God!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, have you ever noticed how hard it is to be a prophet in your own house? We find it easier to listen to a stranger from far away than to the person whom we have known for years. That is the story of today's Gospel. Jesus comes home to Nazareth, to the village where he grew up. On the Sabbath he teaches in the synagogue, and at first the people are amazed. Where did this man get all this? What is this wisdom? (Mark 6:2). But in a moment their amazement turns into offence: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? (Mark 6:3). We know him. We know his family. How can he be anything special?

Dear friends, this is the scandal of the Incarnation. God did not come to us as a thunderbolt, or as a king in a palace. He came as a baby, he grew up in a village, he learned a trade and he worked with his hands. For thirty years nobody noticed anything special. And this is a gift for us. If God became so ordinary, then our ordinary days, our work, our kitchens and our fields are the place where he meets us. But the people of Nazareth could not see him in the ordinary, and Mark says: he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and cured them. He was amazed at their unbelief (Mark 6:5–6). Faith opens the door. Where there is no faith, even the Lord's power does not enter.

In the first reading God sends Ezekiel to a rebellious people. He does not promise him success. He says: whether they hear or refuse to hear, they shall know that there has been a prophet among them (Ezekiel 2:5). What does it mean for us? Each of us, by baptism, is a prophet. In our family, our office, our school, we are asked to speak and live the truth of the Gospel. We may not be listened to. But our task is not to be successful. Our task is to be faithful. God looks after the results.

And what if we are weak? St Paul gives the answer in the second reading. He had a thorn in the flesh, and three times he asked the Lord to remove it. And the Lord said: My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9). Dear friends, each of us has a thorn: an illness, a failure, a sin that we keep repeating, a lonely situation, a child who has left the faith. The Lord may not take it away today. But he promises his grace. And Paul tells us the surprising secret: whenever I am weak, then I am strong. Our weakness is not an obstacle to God. It is the empty space that he fills.

Today, as we receive the Lord in a small piece of bread, let us ask him for three graces: faith that sees him in the ordinary, courage to speak his word whether people hear it or not, and trust in his grace when we are weak. And let us also thank the people at home whom we take for granted. They may be the prophets God has sent us. The Lord who was not honoured in Nazareth is honoured here today. Let us honour him.
kids: Children, Jesus grew up in a village called Nazareth. When he was a grown man he went back there and taught the people about God. They were amazed, and then they said: we know him! He is the carpenter, Mary's son! They did not believe, and Jesus was sad. But he did not give up. He went to other villages and taught them. Today we also learn about St Paul, who had something hard in his life, and God said to him: my grace is enough for you. When something is hard for us, let us remember that Jesus is with us and that his help is enough. And let us always say thank you to the people at home!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the priest Amaziah tells the prophet Amos: go away. Go back to Judah, earn your bread there, and do not prophesy at Bethel. And Amos answers with one of the simplest and bravest sentences in the Bible: I am no prophet, nor a prophet's son; but I am a herdsman, and a dresser of sycamore trees, and the Lord took me from following the flock, and the Lord said to me, Go, prophesy to my people Israel (Amos 7:14–15). He has no title. He has no training. But he has a call, and a call does not need the permission of a king.

Brothers and sisters, God still calls like that. He calls fishermen and tax collectors, farmers and teachers, nurses and drivers, grandmothers who pray the rosary every evening. He does not ask for credentials. He asks: Will you go? And St Paul tells us in the second reading that this call is older than our own lives: he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Before there was a world, God had you in his mind and in his heart. You are not an accident. You are wanted.

In the Gospel Jesus sends out the Twelve. Two by two. Why two? Because the Gospel is not a private opinion; it is a shared life. Because when one is tired, the other holds him up; when one falls, the other lifts him. Think of the families, the couples, the pairs of friends who have carried the Gospel in our own land. And what do they take? A staff and sandals. No bread, no bag, no money. They are dressed like Israel on the night of the Passover, ready to go. They can go anywhere, because they carry nothing but the word.

What will they say? That all should repent. And what will they do? Cast out demons, and anoint with oil many who were sick and heal them. The Church continues this mission. In the sacrament of Anointing of the Sick, in confession, in every Mass, the apostolic work goes on. And you and I are asked to join it in our own small ways: a word, a visit, a prayer, a kindness to someone who is carrying a heavy load.

So this week, let us ask ourselves: what is the Lord sending me to do? What is the staff and sandals I need? And whom will I take with me? Let us go, trusting that the One who sends us is the One who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, the Gospel today tells us that Jesus had twelve special friends, the apostles. He sent them out to tell people about God, and he sent them two by two, so that nobody would be alone. They took only a walking stick and sandals. They did not need to carry anything else, because God would look after them. Jesus wants to send you too! You can bring his love to your school, your friends and your family. You can help a child who is lonely. You can say a prayer for someone who is sick. And it is much more fun when you do it together with a friend!

homily: Dear friends, Moses asks a very honest question: what is his name? He is afraid that when he goes to Egypt the people will ask, and he will have no answer. And God says: I am who I am (Exodus 3:14). It is the most mysterious of all answers. God does not say: I am the strongest, or the greatest. He says: I am. I am here, I am faithful, I am the one who is. And he adds: the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob. His name is joined to the names of a family and a promise.

And listen to what God says next: I have given heed to you and to what has been done to you in Egypt (Exodus 3:16). He has seen. Whoever is suffering today should hear this first: God has seen. And he tells the truth: the king will not let you go unless compelled by a mighty hand (Exodus 3:19). The road will be hard. But God says: I will stretch out my hand. He does not promise an easy road; he promises himself.

And now Jesus, in the Gospel, says almost the same thing in the language of a friend: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest (Matthew 11:28). Who is weary today? Come. Who carries a burden? Come. Not first to an idea or a rule, but to him. And what does he give? Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29). The yoke of two. We do not pull alone.

St Bonaventure, whom we remember today, was one of the most learned men of the Middle Ages, and yet he said that learning must end in love. He had a mind like a library and a heart like a flame, and the flame was fed by the Crucified. Let us do the same: let us study, let us pray, and let us come to the Lord and put our burden on his shoulder. Amen.
kids: Children, Moses asked God: what is your name? And God said: I am. That means: I am always here for you. Then Jesus says to us: Come to me, all who are tired and sad, and I will give you rest. He says: I am kind and gentle. When something is too heavy for you, you can give it to Jesus, like giving your school bag to a big brother to carry! St Bonaventure was a very clever teacher who loved Jesus very much. He taught that the most important thing is to love. Let us tell Jesus today what is heavy for us.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, if you want to know what a shepherd is, imagine a man out on the hillside with a hundred sheep. He knows each by name and he knows which one limps. He walks ahead. At night he counts them, and if one is missing, he goes out into the dark to find it. That is what God says he is in our readings today. Jeremiah is angry at the shepherds who scattered and neglected the flock. But he does not leave it there: I myself will gather the remnant of my flock (Jeremiah 23:3). And in Jesus, God has come to do exactly that.

Psalm 23 gives us the Shepherd's face. He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside still waters, he restores my soul (Psalm 23:2–3). And even in the darkest valley, I fear no evil; for you are with me (Psalm 23:4). Whoever has sat beside a sickbed or a grave knows how much that line means. The Lord does not promise that there will be no valley. He promises that he will be in it with us.

In the second reading St Paul says: he is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). Think of the walls we build: between castes, between families over land, between rich and poor, between parties and communities. Christ has taken down the greatest wall of all, between Jew and Gentile, and made one new humanity. If he can do that, he can do it in our village. The question is whether we are willing to be wall-breakers, or wall-builders.

And then the Gospel. The apostles come back tired, and the first thing Jesus says is: come away and rest a while (Mark 6:31). What a tender Lord! He knows that a good shepherd who does not rest can no longer shepherd. In our month of Karkidakam, when the rain keeps us at home, our elders always said: rest, look after your body, be quiet. Let that be a chance to be with the Lord. But when the crowd is waiting, he does not complain. He had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34). That is the heart of Christ. Let us ask him for it, and let us pray for our shepherds, that they may have it too. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what a shepherd does? He looks after the sheep. He takes them to green grass and cool water. He counts them at night, and if one is lost he goes to find it. The Bible says: the Lord is my shepherd! Jesus is our Good Shepherd. One day his friends came back very tired, and Jesus said: come and rest! But a great crowd of people ran after them, because they needed Jesus so much. Jesus did not send them away. He felt very sorry for them, because they were like sheep with no shepherd, and he taught them. Who looks after you like a shepherd? Your mummy and daddy, your teacher, your priest! Let us say thank you to them today, and pray for them.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, it is a hungry crowd. A man brings twenty small barley loaves to the prophet Elisha in a time of famine. Elisha says: give it to the people. And his servant says what we would all say: how can I set this before a hundred people? (2 Kings 4:43). It is the arithmetic of every hungry place.
