points.apply: At the Lamb of God at Mass, say in your heart the name of one person you wish to entrust to him.

q: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Bring someone to Jesus this week: by prayer, an invitation to Mass, or a lift to confession.

concl: God tests Abraham, stops the knife, and promises that in his offspring all nations will be blessed; the Father later gives his own Son as the Lamb.
Jesus forgives the paralysed man because of his friends' faith, and shows that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.
2027-07-01.resolve: Go to confession this month, and carry one person to God in prayer every day this week.

intro: Theme: “I desire mercy, not sacrifice.”
A grave and a wedding, a pilgrim people comforted by love, and the Heart of Jesus that calls the sinner to his table.

sub: One cave in the land of the promise.
A better country, a heavenly one.
q: “I am a stranger and an alien residing among you; give me property among you for a burying place, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
All of these died in faith without having received the promises, but from a distance they saw and greeted them. They confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth,
points.apply: Pray this week for the dead of your family by name, at the grave or at home.

sub: Isaac walks in the field in the evening.
He looked up, and she looked up.
q: Then Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent. He took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Say aloud to someone in your family this week, “You are a comfort to me.”

sub: He saw a man at the tax booth.
Go and learn: mercy, not sacrifice.
q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
As Jesus was walking along, he saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax booth; and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he got up and followed him.
points.apply: Spend one hour before the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday, and ask the Heart of Jesus to give you a heart like his.

concl: Abraham buries Sarah as a stranger in the land of the promise, and Isaac is comforted by Rebekah's love: the covenant continues through a home built on love.
Jesus calls Matthew and eats with sinners, because he came not for the righteous but for sinners; the Sacred Heart is the heart of that mercy.
2027-07-02.resolve: Keep this First Friday with Mass, confession or adoration, and share a meal with someone who is alone.

intro: Theme: “Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.”
Jacob's stone at Bethel, the Lord who walks beside the runaway, and the touch of faith that reaches the hem of his cloak.

points.h: Surely the Lord is in this place
sub: A runaway with a stone for a pillow.
q: Then Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “Surely the Lord is in this place—and I did not know it!”
Very truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
points.apply: Three times today, in a place you do not think of as holy, say: Surely the Lord is in this place.

sub: Not until I have done what I have promised.
With you always, to the end of the age.
q: Know that I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: If you are far from home or from loved ones, say this promise aloud before you sleep each night this week.

sub: A father with nothing but a request.
A woman who dared only to touch.
The Lord who turns and sees.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and buckler.
Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, “Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.”
points.apply: At each Communion this week, make a conscious act of faith: if I only touch him, I will be made well.

concl: God meets the runaway Jacob on a stone, promises to be with him wherever he goes, and makes the roadside the gate of heaven.
Jesus meets a father and a woman in need, honours the faith of the one who only touches his cloak, and takes the dead girl by the hand.
2027-07-05.resolve: Look for the Lord in the ordinary places you pass through today, and bring one fear to him in prayer.

intro: Theme: “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
Jacob's night at the Jabbok, the compassion of the Shepherd for the harassed crowd, and the harvest that begins on our knees.

points.h: I will not let you go
sub: Alone at the ford in the night.
A new name and a limp.
I have seen God face to face.
q: Then he said, “Let me go, for the day is breaking.” But Jacob said, “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray always and not to lose heart.
points.apply: Pray for one real need for ten minutes a day this week, without giving up.

sub: The shepherd who seeks the lost.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak,
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
points.apply: Look today at one person who seems harassed and helpless, and do one kind thing for them.

sub: A girl of eleven who forgave.
q: Those who go out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, carrying their sheaves.
The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.
points.apply: Say a Hail Mary every day this week for vocations, and ask St Maria Goretti to help the young.

concl: Jacob wrestles all night, refuses to let go until God blesses him, and is given the name Israel, a blessing and a limp.
Jesus has compassion on the harassed crowd, asks us to pray for labourers, and finds a harvest even in an eleven-year-old girl who said no to sin and forgave her killer.
2027-07-06.resolve: Pray each day for ten minutes without giving up, and ask the Lord of the harvest for vocations.

intro: Theme: “The kingdom of heaven has come near.”
A famine, a conscience that wakes, a brother who weeps in secret, and twelve men sent out by Jesus.

sub: The pit has become a throne.
Whom do we go to in need?
q: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.”
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
points.apply: Bring one real need to Jesus in prayer today, and ask what he wants you to do about it.

sub: More than twenty years of silence.
A sin sleeps, it does not die.
q: They said to one another, “Alas, we are paying the penalty for what we did to our brother; we saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this anguish has come upon us.”
If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
points.apply: Make a good examination of conscience this week and go to confession; do not carry the old weight alone.

q: He turned away from them and wept; then he returned and spoke to them.
points.apply: When you must correct or test someone you love, do it as Joseph did: with the aim of bringing them home.

q: Truly the eye of the Lord is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love, to deliver their soul from death, and to keep them alive in famine.
Then Jesus summoned his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to cure every disease and every sickness.
points.apply: Say one sentence this week to someone who is discouraged: God is near you.

concl: God uses famine, a prison and a brother's tears to bring a family back together, and he is patient with a conscience that wakes late.
Jesus calls the Twelve, gives them his own authority and sends them to the lost with the news that the kingdom has come near.
2027-07-07.resolve: Put right one old wrong this week, and speak one word of hope to one person who needs it.

intro: Theme: “You received without payment; give without payment.”
Judah offers himself, Joseph forgives, and the Twelve are sent out with nothing but a gift to give.

sub: The speech that saves a family.
q: Now therefore, please let your servant remain as a slave to my lord in place of the boy; and let the boy go back with his brothers.
No one has greater love than this, to lay down one's life for one's friends.
points.apply: Quietly take one burden off someone near you this week, and do not tell anyone.

q: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” But his brothers could not answer him, so dismayed were they at his presence.
Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
points.apply: Think of the person you find hardest to forgive and pray for them by name every day this week.

sub: God draws good out of it.
q: he had sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose.
points.apply: Write down one hurt in your past and, next to it, one good that God has since brought out of it.

sub: Peace that returns to the giver.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Cure the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, cast out demons. You received without payment; give without payment.
points.apply: Bring a greeting of peace into one house this week: visit a neighbour, a lonely person, a family in trouble.

concl: Judah's repentance and Joseph's forgiveness show how God brings a broken family home and draws good even out of betrayal.
Jesus sends the Twelve with a gift they did not earn and cannot sell, and asks us to give as we have received.
2027-07-08.resolve: Give one gift this week without payment, and forgive one debt that you have been holding.

intro: Theme: “I myself will go down with you.”
Jacob goes down into Egypt with God's promise; Jesus sends his disciples as sheep among wolves, with the Spirit of the Father to speak in them.

points.h: Do not be afraid to go down
q: Then he said, “I am God, the God of your father; do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make of you a great nation there. I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also bring you up again; and Joseph's own hand shall close your eyes.”
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Before the next frightening task or journey, say aloud: Lord, you go down with me.

sub: A life that has seen faithfulness.
q: Israel said to Joseph, “I can die now, having seen for myself that you are still alive.”
Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word;
points.apply: Call or visit an elderly person this week and listen to what God's faithfulness has meant in their life.

points.h: Sheep in the midst of wolves
q: The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord; he is their refuge in the time of trouble.
See, I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves; so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves.
points.apply: Choose prudence and purity together in one real decision this week: neither naive nor cunning.

points.h: It is not you who speak
sub: The martyrs of China and of India.
q: Trust in the Lord, and do good; so you will live in the land, and enjoy security.

When they hand you over, do not worry about how you are to speak or what you are to say; for what you are to say will be given to you at that time; for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
points.apply: Learn the name of one martyr, and pray to them this week for the courage to bear witness.

concl: God calls Jacob by name, promises to go down with him into Egypt and to bring him up again, and so begins the long journey of a people.
Jesus sends his disciples like sheep among wolves and gives them the Spirit of the Father; the martyrs show that the promise holds.
2027-07-09.resolve: Offer one prayer before each important step this week, and pray for persecuted Christians by name.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid.”
Joseph forgives the brothers who still fear him, Genesis ends with a coffin and a promise, and Jesus says three times: have no fear.

sub: What if Joseph still bears a grudge?
Seventeen years of kindness, and still afraid.
q: Realizing that their father was dead, Joseph's brothers said, “What if Joseph still bears a grudge against us and pays us back in full for all the wrong that we did to him?”
But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Make a good confession if you need it, and then let the matter rest: you are forgiven.

points.h: Am I in the place of God?
q: Do not be afraid! Am I in the place of God? Even though you intended to do harm to me, God intended it for good, in order to preserve a numerous people, as he is doing today.
Bear with one another and, if anyone has a complaint against another, forgive each other; just as the Lord has forgiven you, so you also must forgive.
points.apply: Say to one person, in clear and kind words, that you have forgiven them.

sub: Moses and the bones of Joseph.
q: I am about to die; but God will surely come to you, and bring you up out of this land to the land that he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his burial.
points.apply: Think of one promise of God you are waiting for, and say aloud: God will surely come.

sub: Sparrows and the hairs of your head.
q: But now thus says the Lord, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.
points.apply: Choose one fear and hand it to the Father in prayer each morning this week.

concl: Joseph forgives his brothers and sees the larger story God is writing; Genesis ends with his coffin and God's promise to come.
Jesus tells us three times not to be afraid, for the Father knows the sparrows and the hairs of our heads.
2027-07-10.resolve: Hand one old fear to God, and tell one person that you have forgiven them.

intro: Theme: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me.”
A king who forgets, midwives who refuse, a sword that cuts through every loyalty, and a cup of cold water that is never lost.

points.h: A king who did not know Joseph
sub: Forced labour and a river of death.
q: Now a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
points.apply: Thank, this week, one person who did you good long ago.

sub: The Church grows under the cross.
q: But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread, so that the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed;
points.apply: Say no this week to one small injustice that you are asked to go along with.

q: for the son treats the father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; your enemies are members of your own household.
Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword.
points.apply: Name the one loyalty or habit that stands in the way of following Christ, and ask for the courage to put it second.

q: We have escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
points.apply: Give a cup of cold water in some form to a worker or a stranger this week.

concl: A king forgets Joseph and oppresses the Hebrews, but God's blessing grows, and two midwives refuse to obey; Psalm 124 sings: our help is in the name of the Lord.
Jesus asks to be loved above all, promises that we shall find our life by losing it, and says that a cup of cold water given in his name will not lose its reward.
2027-07-12.resolve: Thank one person you have forgotten, and give one act of welcome to a stranger.

intro: Theme: “I drew him out of the water.”
A basket among the reeds, a deliverer not yet recognised, and the Lord's grief over the towns that saw most and turned least.

q: When the child grew up, she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and she took him as her son. She named him Moses, “because,” she said, “I drew him out of the water.”
By faith Moses was hidden by his parents for three months after his birth, because they saw that the child was beautiful; and they were not afraid of the king’s edict.
points.apply: Thank, today, one person who held you up when you could not hold yourself, and ask whom you are holding up.

sub: God's time is longer than ours.
q: He answered, “Who made you a ruler and judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?”
“It was this Moses whom they rejected when they said, ‘Who made you a ruler and a judge?’ and whom God now sent as both ruler and liberator through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
points.apply: Where a good plan of yours has failed, hand it to God again this week and ask what he wants to do with it.

sub: A prophet's lament, not a curse.
q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the deeds of power done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
points.apply: Go to confession this week, and begin the examination of conscience with the question: what have I been given?

sub: Bamberg, and the poor at his table.
q: If a king judges the poor with equity, his throne will be established forever.

It will not be so among you; but whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant, and whoever wishes to be first among you must be your slave; just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
points.apply: Whatever authority you have, at home, at work or in the parish, ask this week how you can use it for the weakest person under it.

concl: God draws Moses out of the water by the hands of three women, and uses a rejected deliverer in his own good time.
Jesus grieves over the towns that received most; the answer to his lament is not fear but a quick, grateful turning back.
2027-07-13.resolve: Thank one person who held you up, and take one concrete step of turning back to the Lord this week.

intro: Theme: “I will be with you.”
A shepherd who turns aside, holy ground that is a sickroom, and the Father who reveals himself to infants.

sub: God speaks to the one who stops.
q: Then Moses said, “I must turn aside and look at this great sight, and see why the bush is not burned up.” When the Lord saw that he had turned aside to see, God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
When Moses saw it, he was amazed at the sight; and as he approached to look, there came the voice of the Lord:
points.apply: Find two quiet minutes today to stop, turn aside and say to God: Here I am.

sub: Ground made holy by God's presence.
q: Then he said, “Come no closer! Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”
Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
points.apply: Be reverent this week in church, and also in the home and the sickroom, because God is present in them.

q: Out of the mouths of babes and infants you have founded a bulwark because of your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
At that time Jesus said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants;
points.apply: Choose one person who is humble and simple in your life and ask what God has taught you through them.

points.h: I was sick and you took care of me
sub: The red cross of the Camillians.
q: Do not hesitate to visit the sick, because for such deeds you will be loved.
I was naked and you gave me clothing, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me.
points.apply: Visit one sick person this week, and take something small to them: a prayer, a fruit, an hour.

concl: God reveals his holiness and his compassion to a shepherd who stops to look, and promises: I will be with you.
The Father reveals himself to the little ones in Jesus, and St Camillus shows that the sickbed is holy ground.
2027-07-14.resolve: Visit one sick person this week, and pray each day: Lord, here I am.

intro: Theme: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.”
The blood on the doorposts and the Lamb, mercy greater than sacrifice, and the little cloud over Carmel that is Mary.

sub: The first month, the first night.
A day of remembrance for ever.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For our paschal lamb, Christ, has been sacrificed.
points.apply: At the next Mass, listen to the words “Behold the Lamb of God” and receive Holy Communion as a Passover.

sub: David and the bread of the Presence.
q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.

I tell you, something greater than the temple is here. But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless. For the Son of Man is lord of the sabbath.
points.apply: This week, let mercy win over a rule once: feed someone, forgive someone, or help someone in need.

sub: Six times nothing, the seventh time a cloud.
Mary, small and humble, who brought the rain of grace.
q: At the seventh time he said, “Look, a little cloud no bigger than a person’s hand is rising out of the sea.”
Then Mary said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.”
points.apply: Pray daily this week, and do not stop at the first “nothing”: go back seven times if you need to.

sub: The scapular as a sign of belonging.
Hearing the word and keeping it.
q: Sing and rejoice, O daughter Zion! For lo, I will come and dwell in your midst, says the Lord.
But he said, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
points.apply: Say a Hail Mary each morning this week, asking: Mother, show me what he wants me to do today.

concl: God passes over his people at the Passover; in Christ, the Lamb, he has saved us, and he desires mercy more than sacrifice.
As a little cloud brought rain to Carmel, Mary brought Jesus to the world, and she teaches us to hear the word and keep it.
2027-07-16.resolve: Each day this week say a Hail Mary to Our Lady of Mount Carmel for a need that is still unanswered, and do one act of mercy.

intro: Theme: “A bruised reed he will not break.”
A night of vigil for a mixed crowd leaving Egypt, and the gentle Servant who does not put out the smoldering wick.

q: That was for the Lord a night of vigil, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. That same night is a vigil to be kept for the Lord by all the Israelites throughout their generations.
Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.
points.apply: Make a ten-minute vigil of prayer before bed this week, and entrust to God someone who is alone tonight.

points.h: A strong hand and an outstretched arm
sub: From Egypt to the Red Sea.
He remembered us in our low estate.
Rescued from the power of darkness.
q: and brought Israel out from among them, for his steadfast love endures forever; with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for his steadfast love endures forever;
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Make a list of three rescues in your own life, and thank God for each of them aloud.

sub: Other slaves and strangers went out too.
The Gentiles will hope in his name.
q: for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God,
points.apply: Greet and get to know one newcomer or stranger in your parish or workplace this week.

sub: The Servant who does not wrangle or cry aloud.
The smoldering wick he will not quench.
q: He will not cry or lift up his voice, or make it heard in the street; a bruised reed he will not break, and a dimly burning wick he will not quench; he will faithfully bring forth justice.
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind,
points.apply: Visit or phone someone who is discouraged, and offer them encouragement, not advice.

concl: The Lord keeps vigil to bring his people out of Egypt, and a mixed crowd goes out with them: his people is wider than one family.
Jesus answers plotting with healing; the gentle Servant does not break the bruised reed, and in his name the nations hope.
2027-07-17.resolve: Welcome one stranger and encourage one discouraged person this week, and keep a short vigil of prayer one evening.

intro: Theme: “The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to keep still.”
The sea in front, the army behind, and the sign that is greater than Jonah.

points.h: Do not be afraid, stand firm
q: But Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the Lord will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians whom you see today you shall never see again.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Choose the fear that troubles you most, and say Moses' words over it every morning this week.

sub: Why do you cry out to me?
A time to stand, a time to walk.
The God who opens a path.
q: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as if it were dry land, but when the Egyptians attempted to do so they were drowned.
points.apply: After praying about your difficulty, take one practical step today, and do not wait for the whole path to be clear.

sub: Three days in the heart of the earth.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Go to Mass this week, not to ask for a sign but to receive the One who is the sign.

concl: God opened a path through the sea for Israel and told Moses to lead the people forward; he asks us for trust and for a step.
Jesus gives the sign of Jonah, his death and Resurrection; something greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.
2027-07-19.resolve: Each day this week name one fear, say Moses' words over it, and take one step.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.”
The night of the sea, the faith that was born from a rescue, and the family that the Lord gathers around his Father's will.

points.h: Through the sea on dry ground
sub: The wall of water on either side.
The pillar that terrifies the pursuers.
q: The Israelites went into the sea on dry ground, the waters forming a wall for them on their right and on their left.
I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross with holy water slowly each time you enter a church this week, and remember your baptism.

sub: The sea is not the goal.
q: Israel saw the great work that the Lord did against the Egyptians. So the people feared the Lord and believed in the Lord and in his servant Moses.
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Write down one moment when God rescued you, and thank him for it at Mass on Sunday.

points.h: My brother and sister and mother
sub: The family of the Father's will.
Mary, the first to hear and obey.
q: If my father and mother forsake me, the Lord will take me up.
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
points.apply: Do one thing this week for someone who has no family nearby: a call, a visit, a meal.

concl: The Lord brings Israel through the sea, and the people believe in him and sing; in baptism he has brought us through the same waters.
Jesus calls those who do the Father's will his own family, and Mary, who said yes first, stands at the head of that family.
2027-07-20.resolve: Each day this week do one thing that you know the Father asks of you, and thank him for the family of faith.

intro: Theme: “Let anyone with ears listen!”
Bread from heaven for the body, the word from heaven for the heart, and the Sower who scatters it everywhere.

sub: The first hint of the Sabbath.
q: Then the Lord said to Moses, “I am going to rain bread from heaven for you, and each day the people shall go out and gather enough for that day.
Give us this day our daily bread.
points.apply: Say the grace before meals slowly this week, and remember a hungry family by name.

sub: Man hu, the origin of the name manna.
q: he rained down on them manna to eat, and gave them the grain of heaven.
Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
points.apply: Next Sunday, listen to the Gospel of the bread of life with the manna in mind, and receive Communion with thanks.

points.h: A sower went out to sow
sub: Path, rock, thorns and good soil.
The word that does not return empty.
q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
Other seeds fell on good soil and brought forth grain, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
points.apply: Name the thorns that choke the word in you, a worry, an addiction, a distraction, and take one step to cut them back.

points.h: A light for the mind, a fire for the will
sub: Holding it fast and bearing fruit.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
points.apply: Read one Gospel passage slowly every day this week, and write down one thing it asks of you.

concl: God feeds his hungry people with bread from heaven, enough for each day, and asks them to trust.
Jesus the Sower scatters the word generously; may our hearts be good soil, as St Lawrence of Brindisi taught by his preaching.
2027-07-21.resolve: Every day this week read the Gospel slowly, receive your daily bread with thanks, and share some of it.

intro: Theme: “I have seen the Lord.”
A woman who sought him in the dark, was called by name, and was sent to the apostles with the first Easter news.

sub: The Song of Songs: rising to search.
A garden and an empty tomb.
q: Upon my bed at night I sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him, but found him not; I called him, but he gave no answer.
Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the tomb.
points.apply: Choose one prayer to say at the start of the day this week, and say it before the light comes.

sub: A love ready to carry the body.
q: O God, you are my God, I seek you, my soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you, as in a dry and weary land where there is no water.
They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.”
points.apply: Stay beside someone who is grieving this week, in silence if necessary, and let them know they are not alone.

sub: The voice that calls us out of grief.
q: But now thus says the Lord, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence before the tabernacle or with the Gospel, and let the Lord say your name.

q: I shall not die, but I shall live, and recount the deeds of the Lord.
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, in your own words, what the risen Lord has done for you.

concl: Mary Magdalene stays at the tomb, is called by name, and is sent by the risen Lord to his brothers: the first witness of the Resurrection.
The Church keeps her day as a feast, and calls her the apostle of the apostles; with her we say: I have seen the Lord.
2027-07-22.resolve: Each day this week listen for the Lord calling you by name, and tell someone one thing he has done for you.

intro: Theme: “The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul.”
The gift before the command, the law sweeter than honey, and the seed that must be received into the heart.

sub: I am the Lord your God.
Out of the house of slavery.
Ten words for a people at liberty.
q: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; you shall have no other gods before me.
If you love me, you will keep my commandments.
points.apply: Read Exodus 20:1–17 slowly this week, and thank God for the freedom that the law protects.

sub: More to be desired than gold.
On these two commandments hang all the law.
q: The law of the Lord is perfect, reviving the soul; the decrees of the Lord are sure, making wise the simple;

He said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the greatest and first commandment. And a second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.”
points.apply: Do one act of love for God and one for your neighbor each day this week.

sub: The law written on the heart.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
But as for what was sown on good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, in one case a hundredfold, in another sixty, and in another thirty.
points.apply: Choose one commandment and ask yourself each evening: how did I keep it today?

points.h: A mother, a widow, a mystic
sub: Delight in the law, day and night.
The thorns of the court did not choke the word.
q: but their delight is in the law of the Lord, and on his law they meditate day and night. They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
As for what was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, but the cares of the world and the lure of wealth choke the word, and it yields nothing.
points.apply: Name the thorn, a worry or a desire, that most chokes God's word in you, and ask St Bridget to pray for you.

concl: God gives his law as a gift to freed people; the psalm sings its sweetness, and Jesus fulfils it in love.
The seed of the word must be received into good soil; St Bridget shows what a heart looks like in which the word takes root.
2027-07-23.resolve: Each day this week give the word of God a fixed hour, and ask the Lord to write his law on your heart.

intro: Theme: “See the blood of the covenant.”
We will do, the blood of the covenant, the patient householder, and the hidden prayer of a hermit.

q: Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord and all the ordinances; and all the people answered with one voice, and said, “All the words that the Lord has spoken we will do.”
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: After Mass on Sunday, name one thing you heard and will do this week, and do it.

sub: Half on the altar, half on the people.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
He said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
points.apply: At Communion this Sunday, say silently: Lord, I belong to your covenant, and I will do what you say.

q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Pray by name this week for someone you have judged harshly, asking God to give them time and you patience.

sub: Your Father who is in secret.
q: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call on me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Take ten minutes of silence each day this week and pray for Lebanon and for peace.

concl: God seals a covenant with his people in blood at Sinai, and in Christ he seals the new covenant in the Eucharist: we say we will do, and we are called to do it.
The Lord is patient with the wheat and the weeds; St Sharbel shows how a life hidden in prayer bears fruit for many.
2027-07-24.resolve: Each day this week do one thing you have heard from the word, be patient with someone, and keep ten minutes of silence.

intro: Theme: “A faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice.”
Moses in the breach, the mustard seed, and the hidden grandparents of Jesus: faith is always handed on.

sub: The calf, the broken tablets, Aaron's excuse.
Blot me out of the book.
q: Had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn away his wrath from destroying them.
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Name one person far from God, and pray for them every day this week, asking to stand in the breach for them.

sub: The smallest of all the seeds.
Yeast hidden in three measures of flour.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.

He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field; it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.”
points.apply: Do one small good thing today that no one will notice, and trust God to make it grow.

q: We will not hide them from their children; we will tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the Lord, and his might, and the wonders that he has done.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Tell one young person this week how you came to believe, and thank the one who first taught you to pray.

concl: Moses shows the heart of an intercessor, who puts his own name on the line for a people who failed.
The kingdom grows from small, hidden beginnings, like the faith that Joachim and Anne handed on to Mary and she to the world.
2027-07-26.resolve: Pray each day for someone far from God, and tell a younger person one story of faith from your family.

intro: Theme: “The Lord, the Lord, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger.”
The tent of meeting, the name of the Lord, and the patient farmer: God speaks as to a friend and waits for the harvest.

points.h: Face to face, as to a friend
q: Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend.

I do not call you servants any longer, because the servant does not know what the master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
points.apply: Choose a fixed time and place for a quiet talk with God each day this week, and keep it.

q: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Go to confession this week and let the God who is slow to anger forgive you, then forgive one person who has wronged you.

sub: Let both grow until the harvest.
The righteous will shine like the sun.
q: Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Let anyone with ears listen!
points.apply: Be patient this week with one person you have been quick to judge, and look for the good seed in them.

concl: God speaks to Moses as to a friend and proclaims his name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love.
Jesus explains that the field is the world and that the harvest belongs to the Lord, so that we may use our time to sow good seed and turn to him.
2027-07-27.resolve: Spend ten minutes a day this week talking to God as to a friend, and be patient with one difficult person.

intro: Theme: “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”
A shining face, a pearl of great value and a hidden life: St Alphonsa shows what happens when a person finds the treasure.

points.h: A face that shines without knowing
sub: Moses has been talking with God.
Transformed from one degree of glory to another.
q: When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil on his face.

And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another; for this comes from the Lord, the Spirit.
points.apply: Give some time each day this week to be quietly with the Lord, and let the light of that time reach someone else.

sub: In his joy he sells all.
Everything is loss compared with knowing Christ.
q: if you seek it like silver, and search for it as for hidden treasures
More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.
points.apply: Ask the Lord what he wants you to give up this week so that you may hold him more fully, and do it with joy.

sub: A hidden life of illness and prayer.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy. Those who go out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, carrying their sheaves.
Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Offer one daily difficulty, a tiredness, a delay, a pain, for a person you name, and trust that nothing offered in love is lost.

concl: Moses shows that those who speak with God carry his light, and that the saints are people through whom it reaches others.
St Alphonsa found the pearl, gave all, and offered her hidden sufferings for others, so that her life, like the grain of wheat, bears much fruit in Kerala and the world.
2027-07-28.resolve: Offer one hidden difficulty each day this week for someone by name, and be gentle with one person who tries your patience.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life.”
The tent where God lives, Martha's faith, and Mary's better part: three friends of Jesus and the home where he was welcome.

sub: The tabernacle set up as the Lord commanded.
The Word pitched his tent among us.
q: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament this week and say to the Lord: you are here, and I believe it.

sub: Lord, if you had been here.
I know he will rise on the last day.
You are the Messiah, the Son of God.
q: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the earth; and after my skin has been thus destroyed, then in my flesh I shall see God.
She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.”
points.apply: Bring to Jesus, in honest words like Martha's, one loss or sorrow in your life, and then say: I believe.

sub: Martha welcomed him into her home.
q: One thing I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in his temple.
But the Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things; there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.”
points.apply: Put aside ten minutes each day this week, with no distraction, to listen to a Gospel passage.

concl: God's dwelling among his people reaches its fullness in the Word made flesh, who found a home in the house at Bethany.
Martha's faith, Mary's listening and Lazarus's silent witness show how we welcome the Lord who is the resurrection and the life.
2027-07-29.resolve: Welcome Jesus into your home each day this week with ten minutes of quiet listening, and serve one person with love.

intro: Theme: “Prophets are not without honor except in their own country and in their own house.”
God's appointed feasts, Christ the first fruits, and the Nazareth that did not recognise him: holy time and fresh eyes.

sub: The appointed festivals of the Lord.
God meets his people at fixed hours.
q: These are the appointed festivals of the Lord, the holy convocations, which you shall celebrate at the time appointed for them.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
points.apply: Keep one fixed time of prayer every day this week, and make it a meeting, not a task.

sub: The sheaf raised on the day after the sabbath.
Fifty days to the new grain.
Christ the first fruits of the dead.
q: When you enter the land that I am giving you and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the sheaf of the first fruits of your harvest to the priest.
But in fact Christ has been raised from the dead, the first fruits of those who have died.
points.apply: Offer to God the first fruits of your week: the first minutes of the morning, the first share of your income, the first act of kindness.

sub: Is not this the carpenter's son?
Not many deeds of power, because of unbelief.
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.
He came to what was his own, and his own people did not accept him. But to all who received him, who believed in his name, he gave power to become children of God.
points.apply: At Mass this week, look at the host with the eyes of someone seeing Jesus for the first time, and receive him with faith.

concl: God appoints times to meet his people, and in Christ the first fruits of the harvest of the dead the festivals find their fulfilment.
In Nazareth familiarity closed their eyes; the Lord asks us for the faith that sees him in the ordinary.
2027-07-30.resolve: Keep a fixed time of prayer each day this week, and look at the Mass and your neighbours with fresh eyes.

intro: Theme: “Whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.”
The year of Jubilee, a king enslaved by fear and a prophet at liberty in prison, and St Ignatius: liberty is to give oneself wholly to God.

sub: Seven weeks of years, and the trumpet.
Return to your property and family.
q: And you shall hallow the fiftieth year and you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants.

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor.”
points.apply: Forgive one debt or grievance this week, and so give someone a small Jubilee.

sub: It is not lawful for you to have her.
Herod fears the crowd and the guests.
John's disciples go and tell Jesus.
q: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they abhor the one who speaks the truth.
For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
points.apply: Speak one honest and kind word this week where silence would be easier, and bring any sadness about it to Jesus in prayer.

points.h: For the greater glory of God
sub: The Society of Jesus and the road to India.
q: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with a short offering: Lord, all for your greater glory.

concl: The Jubilee proclaims that God releases his people, restores what was lost and keeps every family at home in the land.
St Ignatius found freedom in giving himself wholly to God, and shows that whatever we do can be done for his glory.
2027-07-31.resolve: Begin each day with the offering: for the greater glory of God, and forgive one person who has wronged you.
